definition.name: Group Messaging Application
definition.overview:
A **Group Messaging Application** is a messaging application organized around the **group**: a conversation among a set of known people that the members themselves assemble and manage, exchanging messages in one shared, persistent stream.

The defining core is deliberately small — three structures:

```text
Member-defined participant set
(the group of known people is assembled and changed by its own members)
└── Shared message stream addressed to the group
    (all members see the same stream; every message carries sender attribution)
    └── Persistent shared history
        (the stream is retained and available to members over time)
```

Everything else commonly associated with group chat — group names and avatars, member rosters, admin roles, share links and join approvals, photo albums or polls — is standard equipment in mature products but is not what makes a product a group messaging application. Carrier-era group texts, SMS-backed class groups, and modern app-based group chats all satisfy the same core without any of those specifics.

The group, not the person-to-person thread, is the unit users create, join, and manage. When that emphasis flips — when personal conversations are the center and groups are one thread type among them — the product belongs to Instant Messaging. The boundary is a gradient and is described below.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **群组消息应用** 是围绕 **群组** 组织起来的消息应用：一组已知人士之间的对话，由成员自身组建和管理，在一个共享的、持久化的消息流中交换消息。

其定义性核心是刻意精简的——仅包含三个结构：

```text
成员定义的参与者集合
（已知人士的群组由其自身成员组建和更改）
└── 面向群组的共享消息流
    （所有成员看到的是相同的消息流；每条消息都携带发送者信息）
    └── 持久化的共享历史记录
        （消息流被保留，供成员随时查看）
```

其他通常与群组聊天相关的东西——群组名称和头像、成员名单、管理员角色、分享链接和加入审核、相册或投票——是成熟产品中的标准配置，但这些并不是一个产品成为群组消息应用的核心。运营商时代的群发短信、基于SMS的班级群组，以及现代基于应用的群组聊天，都满足了相同的核心，即使没有这些具体功能。

群组，而非点对点对话线程，是用户创建、加入和管理的基本单位。当这个重点发生反转——当个人对话成为中心，而群组只是其中的一种对话类型时——该产品就属于即时消息。这条界线是渐变的，下文将对此进行描述。
definition.dc:
Three structures, each with a removal test:

- **Member-defined participant set.** The conversation exists because someone brought specific people together — the group's membership is created and changed by its own members (or its owner), through invitations and member-management actions. Remove this and the membership becomes self-service by address (that is a chat room), assigned by an organization's roster (that is team messaging), or governed by a community container (that is community chat).
- **Shared message stream addressed to the group.** Messages are sent to the group and visible to all of its members as one stream, with each message attributed to its sender. This is what makes it a group *conversation* rather than a broadcast: if recipients receive only individual copies and cannot see each other's responses, the shared stream is gone and the product stops being a group conversation (this degenerate form exists — carrier group SMS is the canonical example — and is documented by its own vendors as the limited fallback).
- **Persistent shared history.** The stream survives the live session; members can scroll back to earlier context, and history remains available as members come and go. Remove persistence and the surface becomes ephemeral live chat.
definition.dc_zh: 成员定义的参与者集：对话的存在是因为某人聚集了特定的人——群组的成员资格由其自身成员（或所有者）通过邀请和成员管理操作创建和更改。移除此点后，成员资格将变为按地址自助（即聊天室）、由组织名单分配（即团队消息）或由社区容器管理（即社区聊天）。共享的消息流针对群组：消息发送给群组，并作为单一流对所有成员可见，每条消息归因于其发送者。这使其成为群组对话而非广播：如果接收者只收到单独副本且无法看到彼此的响应，共享流消失，产品不再是群组对话（这种退化形式存在——运营商群组短信是典型例子——并被其供应商记录为有限回退）。持久化的共享历史：流在实时会话后仍然存在；成员可以回滚到早期上下文，历史在成员进出时保持可用。移除持久性后，表面变为短暂的实时聊天。
definition.rules:
- **Membership is member-shaped.** The normal path into a group runs through its members — an invitation, a member-shared link, or a member-gated request. Open discovery of groups by address is not the default posture; where a product allows listing groups to be found, it is an owner-controlled opt-in rather than the norm.
- **One stream, not copies.** Every member sees the same shared stream. Forms that send each recipient a private copy (carrier group SMS being the documented example) fall outside the shared-stream core, and their own vendors treat them as the limited fallback.
- **History persists; deletion is explicit.** Clearing history, leaving, and ending are distinct operations with different scopes — personal view, personal exit, and whole-group deletion. Ending a group deletes it for everyone and, in the products that offer it, cannot be undone.
- **Roles gate destructive or structural actions.** Editing the group's identity, changing join rules, removing members, transferring ownership, and ending the group are owner/admin actions where roles exist; peer groups without roles leave most of these choices to whoever acts first.
- **Identity is scoped to the group.** A member can present a different name or photo inside one group than in another; the group's roster, not a global directory, is the identity context.
- **Exit differs by how you left.** Someone who left voluntarily can typically rejoin themselves; someone who was removed needs a current member to let them back in.
definition.rules_zh:
- **成员资格由成员塑造。** 进入群组的正常路径需通过其成员——邀请、成员分享的链接或由成员把关的申请。按地址公开发现群组并非默认姿态；当产品允许列出群组供人发现时，这是由所有者控制的可选功能，而非常态。
- **一个共享流，而非多个副本。** 每位成员看到的都是同一个共享消息流。那种向每个接收者发送私有副本的形式（运营商群发SMS是有据可查的例子）不属于共享流核心，其供应商也将其视为有限的备选方案。
- **历史持久化；删除是明确操作。** 清除历史记录、离开和结束是具有不同范围的不同操作——个人视图、个人退出和整个群组删除。结束群组意味着为所有人删除它，在提供该功能的产品中，此操作无法撤销。
- **角色管控破坏性或结构性操作。** 在存在角色的群组中，编辑群组身份、更改加入规则、移除成员、转让所有权和结束群组是所有者/管理员的操作；没有角色的平等群组则将这些选择权留给第一个采取行动的人。
- **身份限定于群组范围。** 成员在一个群组中可以展示与另一个群组不同的名称或照片；群组的成员名单，而非全局通讯录，是身份识别的语境。
- **退出方式取决于离开的原因。** 自愿离开的人通常可以自行重新加入；被移除的人则需要现有成员将其重新邀请进来。

definition.name: Instant Messaging Application
definition.overview:
An **Instant Messaging Application** enables private or small-group message exchange between individually addressable participants, retained as persistent conversation history.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Personal Addressable Identity
└── Reachability between specific known participants
    └── Conversation thread (1:1 or member-defined small group)
        └── Message
            └── Persistent conversation history
```

Everything commonly associated with modern consumer IM — phone-number identity, address-book sync, delivery receipts, media, voice / video calls, presence, multi-device sync — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. Older, regional, platform-native and social-graph IM products also fit this definition without any of those specifics.

When the dominant surface shifts to organizational channels, public discovery, broadcast, or social feed, the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (Team Messaging, Community Chat Platform, Social Live Streaming, Social Network).
definition.overview_zh:
一个**即时消息应用程序**允许个别可寻址参与者之间的私密或小组消息交换，保留为持久化的对话历史。

定义结构很小：

```text
个人可寻址身份
└── 特定已知参与者之间的可达性
    └── 对话线程（1:1或成员定义的小组）
        └── 消息
            └── 持久化的对话历史
```

所有与现代消费者IM相关的常见功能——电话号码身份、通讯录同步、送达回执、媒体、语音/视频通话、在线状态、多设备同步——在当前产品中很普遍，但不是定义核心的一部分。较旧的、区域性的、平台原生的和社交图谱IM产品也符合此定义，即使没有这些具体功能。

当主导界面转向组织频道、公共发现、广播或社交信息流时，该产品正漂向不同的应用程序类型（团队消息、社区聊天平台、社交直播、社交网络）。
definition.dc:
```text
Personal Addressable Identity
└── Reachability between specific known participants
    └── Conversation thread (1:1 or member-defined small group)
        └── Message
            └── Persistent conversation history
```

Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as IM:

- **Personal addressable identity** — every participant is an individually identifiable person, reachable in the product's identity space. Without this, the product becomes a broadcast / channel surface.
- **Reachability between specific known participants** — the conversation graph is built from the personal contact graph, not from public discovery. Without this, the product becomes a community / discovery surface.
- **Conversation thread between identified participants** — messages belong to a thread bound to specific participants, not to a public topic or feed.
- **Persistent conversation history** — the thread survives the live session; later participants can read earlier messages. Without persistence, the product becomes an ephemeral live surface.
definition.dc_zh:
个人可寻址身份
└── 特定已知参与者间的可达性
    └── 对话线程（1:1 或成员定义的小群体）
        └── 消息
            └── 持久化对话历史
definition.rules:
### Delivery state is user-visible

Unlike many Application Types, IM exposes the transport state of a message directly to the sender — sent / delivered / read. This is a defining user-facing behavior. Some products allow the user to disable read receipts; the conceptual model stays the same.

### Conversation threads are durable

Threads survive the live session. The user can return later and find the history. This is in deliberate contrast with ephemeral live or story-style surfaces.

### Message lifecycle

A message is subject to the lifecycle that the product offers (edit, delete, forward, reply, react, optionally disappear on a timer). Exact features vary by product; some are standard, others optional.

### Presence privacy

Most products allow the user to control who sees online / last-seen, typing, and read receipts. This is a structural privacy surface, not an afterthought.

### The contact list is the reachability graph

The user cannot normally message someone outside their reachability graph. This makes the graph both a UX surface and an access-control surface.
definition.rules_zh:
### 送达状态对用户可见

与许多应用程序类型不同，IM直接向发送者暴露消息的传输状态——已发送/已送达/已读。这是一个定义性的用户面向行为。一些产品允许用户禁用已读回执；概念模型保持不变。

### 对话线程是持久的

线程在实时会话后仍然存在。用户可以稍后返回并找到历史记录。这与短暂的实时或故事风格界面形成有意对比。

### 消息生命周期

消息受产品提供的生命周期约束（编辑、删除、转发、回复、反应、可选定时消失）。具体功能因产品而异；有些是标准的，有些是可选的。

### 在线状态隐私

大多数产品允许用户控制谁可以看到在线/最后在线、输入状态和已读回执。这是一个结构性的隐私界面，而不是事后考虑。

### 联系人列表是可达性图

用户通常不能向其可达性图之外的人发送消息。这使得该图既是UX界面，也是访问控制界面。

definition.name: Disposable Email Service
definition.overview:
A **Disposable Email Service** provides a working email address that can be obtained instantly, without registration or personal details, together with a self-contained inbox where mail sent to that address is received and read — and which exists to be used briefly and then abandoned.

The problem it solves is exposure: many everyday actions (signing up for a website, downloading a trial, posting in a forum, making a one-off purchase) demand an email address, and the address given out becomes a channel for marketing mail, tracking, and — if the recipient is breached — a path to the user's real mailbox. A disposable email service lets the user hand out an address they do not care about, receive whatever the sender sends, act on it, and walk away.

The defining core is deliberately small — three properties that hold across the whole researched market:

- **Identity-free issuance** — the address is available to anyone who visits the service (or calls its API). No account, no password setup as a precondition, no personal data.
- **Self-contained inbox** — mail to the address is received *inside the service*, in an inbox the service exposes directly. The service does not merely forward mail on to the user's real mailbox.
- **Disposability by design** — the address and its inbox are not meant to persist. Their lifetime is bounded by the product (a countdown, a session, a retention window) or ends when the user deletes or abandons them. Leaving costs nothing.

Remove the first property and the product is ordinary webmail. Remove the second and it is an email aliasing/forwarding service. Remove the third and it is mailbox hosting. All three together are what makes this a distinct Type.
definition.overview_zh:
一种**一次性电子邮件服务**提供即时可用的电子邮件地址，无需注册或提供个人信息，并附带一个独立的收件箱，用于接收和阅读发送至该地址的邮件——其设计初衷即为短暂使用后随即被遗弃。

它解决的问题是隐私暴露：许多日常操作（注册网站、下载试用版、在论坛发帖、进行一次性购买）都要求提供电子邮件地址，而泄露的地址会成为营销邮件、追踪以及——若接收方数据泄露——通往用户真实邮箱的路径。一次性电子邮件服务允许用户提供一个他们并不在意的地址，接收发送者发送的任何内容，完成操作后便离开。

其定义性核心刻意保持精简——在整个研究市场中普遍存在的三个属性：

- **无身份发行**——任何访问该服务（或调用其 API）的人均可获取地址。无需账户，无需预先设置密码，无需个人数据。
- **独立收件箱**——发送至该地址的邮件在*服务内部*的收件箱中接收，该收件箱由服务直接暴露。服务并非仅将邮件转发至用户的真实邮箱。
- **设计上的可丢弃性**——地址及其收件箱并非旨在持久存在。其生命周期受产品限制（倒计时、会话、保留窗口）或在用户删除或遗弃时结束。离开没有任何成本。

移除第一个属性，该产品即为普通网络邮件。移除第二个属性，它即为电子邮件别名/转发服务。移除第三个属性，它即为邮箱托管。三者结合才构成了这一独特的类型。
definition.dc:
```text
Temporary Address
  └── Inbox (held by the service)
        └── Message
              └── (read, act on, download, expire)
definition.dc_zh:
临时地址
  └── 收件箱（由服务方托管）
        └── 邮件
              └── （阅读、处理、下载、过期）
definition.rules:
### Access follows knowledge, not identity

Because issuance requires no identity, inbox access is typically granted to whoever possesses the address (or its generated password or inbox identifier). Privacy in this Type comes from the address being *unknown and temporary*, not from an account boundary. Products mitigate this with generated per-mailbox passwords, "scrambled" address variants, or private custom domains — an important variant dimension, but the knowledge-based baseline is common to the Type.

### Receive-centric

The core act is receiving. Sending from the disposable address is uncommon and, where it exists, a secondary surface. Users do not build correspondence history here — the inbox holds transient content, not relationships.

### Disposal is automatic by default

Messages and mailboxes end without the user asking: through timers, session ends, or retention windows, or through explicit delete/forget actions. Some products allow an address to persist indefinitely if kept, but nothing in the Type assumes or encourages permanence, and the user's real identity is never attached to the inbox.

### The ecosystem pushes back

Recipients of disposable addresses — signup systems and mail senders — commonly maintain lists of disposable domains and reject them. This adversarial dynamic is built into the Type's reality: products respond with rotating domains that periodically change, sub-address tricks that inherit a deliverable main address, custom domains, and guidance about which of their domains work best for short-term versus long-term use. Products in this market also acknowledge delivery friction (a confirmation mail that arrives late or never) — one reason some offer forwarding to a real mailbox as a fallback.

### Abuse is managed, not invited

Because the service is anonymous by design, products impose their own boundaries: inbound spam filtering, rate limits on APIs and public domains, terms prohibiting illegal use and resale of the service, and technical measures against automated scraping. The anonymous surface is for the user's identity, not for unlimited free infrastructure.
definition.rules_zh:
### 访问基于认知，而非身份

由于发行无需身份，收件箱访问通常授予拥有该地址（或其生成的密码或收件箱标识符）的人。此类型的隐私来自地址的*未知性和临时性*，而非账户边界。产品通过生成每邮箱密码、“混淆”地址变体或私有自定义域名来缓解此问题——这是一个重要的变体维度，但基于认知的基线是该类型的共性。

### 以接收为中心

核心行为是接收。从一次性地址发送不常见，且即使存在，也是次要功能。用户在此处不建立通信历史——收件箱保存的是临时内容，而非关系。

### 默认自动处置

消息和邮箱在用户未请求的情况下结束：通过计时器、会话结束、保留窗口，或通过明确的删除/遗忘操作。某些产品允许地址在保留时无限期存在，但该类型中没有任何内容假设或鼓励永久性，且用户的真实身份永远不会附加到收件箱上。

### 生态系统产生反制

一次性地址的接收方——注册系统和邮件发送者——通常维护一次性域名列表并拒绝它们。这种对抗性动态内建于该类型的现实：产品通过定期更换的轮换域名、继承可交付主地址的子地址技巧、自定义域名，以及关于其域名在短期与长期使用中哪个效果最佳的指导来应对。该市场中的产品也承认交付摩擦（确认邮件延迟到达或从未到达）——这是某些产品提供转发至真实邮箱作为后备方案的原因之一。

### 滥用受到管控，而非被邀请

definition.name: Internet Calling Application
definition.overview:
An **Internet Calling Application** is a personal application whose central act is a real-time voice call between specific people, carried over the internet by the service itself rather than over the telephone voice channel.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Personal Calling Identity
└── Reachable specific people (contacts / recents)
    └── Real-time voice call (place → ring → answer → talk → end)
        └── Live two-way audio over the internet
```

Everything commonly associated with modern calling apps — call logs, video, group calls, voicemail, spam filtering, dial pads for calling regular phone numbers — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. Older products (early-2000s desktop voice chat, account-based calling services) fit this definition without any of those specifics.

When the primary surface becomes a registered telephony line with desk-phone semantics, the product is a Softphone. When the primary medium becomes video, it drifts toward the Video Calling Application Type. When calls become scheduled multi-party meetings with bridges and host controls, it becomes Conference Calling.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**互联网通话应用**是一种个人应用，其核心行为是特定人员之间的实时语音通话，该通话由服务本身通过互联网承载，而非通过传统电话语音信道。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
个人通话身份
└── 可触达的特定人员（联系人 / 最近通话）
     └── 实时语音通话（拨出 → 响铃 → 接听 → 通话 → 结束）
         └── 通过互联网进行的实时双向音频
```

现代通话应用通常关联的一切——通话记录、视频、群组通话、语音信箱、垃圾电话过滤、用于拨打普通电话号码的拨号盘——在当前产品中虽已普及，但并不属于定义性核心。较旧的产品（2000年代初的桌面语音聊天、基于账户的通话服务）符合此定义，而不具备上述任何具体特性。

当主要界面变为具有桌面电话语义的注册电信线路时，该产品即为软电话（Softphone）。当主要媒介变为视频时，它趋向于视频通话应用类型。当通话变为带有桥接和主持人控制的预定多方会议时，它变为会议通话。
definition.dc:
```text
Personal Calling Identity
└── Reachable specific people (contacts / recents)
    └── Real-time voice call (place → ring → answer → talk → end)
        └── Live two-way audio over the internet
```

Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as an internet calling application:

- **Personal calling identity** — every participant is an individually identifiable person, addressable in the service's identity space. Without this, the product becomes an anonymous or room-based audio surface.
- **Reachable specific people** — the call target is a specific known person drawn from the application's own people surface (contacts, recent calls), not a public room, a scheduled bridge, or a random pairing. Without this, the product becomes a conference bridge or a random-chat surface.
- **The call as a stateful real-time event** — a call is placed, rings, is answered or declined, is active while both parties are simultaneously present, and ends. Synchronous co-presence is what separates a call from an asynchronous voice message.
- **Live two-way audio over the internet** — the medium and the transport. The service itself carries the call; this is what separates an internet calling application from a telephone dialer.
definition.dc_zh:
个人通话身份
└── 可联系的具体人员（联系人/最近通话）
    └── 实时语音通话（拨打 → 响铃 → 接听 → 通话 → 结束）
        └── 通过互联网的实时双向音频
definition.rules:
### Calls require synchronous co-presence

A call exists only while both (all) parties are simultaneously connected. If the callee does not answer, the event does not disappear: it becomes a missed call, and optionally a voicemail. This is the structural difference from messaging, where the exchange persists without both parties being present.

### The answer act is explicit

Ringing is a request, not a connection. The callee accepts or declines; declining can carry structured responses (message, callback reminder, voicemail). A second incoming call during a live call forces an explicit choice: end-and-accept, hold-and-accept, or decline.

### Calls are logged

Completed, missed, and declined calls leave entries in the call log. The log is user-visible and actionable (call back), and in mature products it is filterable (all / missed / unknown callers).

### Identity gates reachability

The user can normally call only people present in the service's identity space (their contacts or the service's user base). This makes the people surface both a UX surface and an access boundary. Products differ in how strangers are handled — some filter or silence unknown callers, some allow blocking.

### Video is the same call, not a different object

A video call shares the identity, the log entry, and the lifecycle of an audio call; it can be answered as audio, and audio calls can be upgraded. Products that make video the default mode are drifting toward the Video Calling Application Type, but the underlying call object is the same.

### Breakout calling is metered where present

Calling regular landline or mobile numbers is, where offered, the paid layer of the service (credit, subscriptions, or inbound numbers), distinct from the free person-to-person calling that defines the Type.
definition.rules_zh:
### 通话需要同步共在

通话仅在所有各方同时连接时存在。如果被叫方不接听，该事件不会消失：它变为未接来电，并可选地变为语音信箱。这是与消息传递的结构差异，在消息传递中，交换在双方不在场的情况下持续存在。

### 接听行为是显式的

响铃是一个请求，而非连接。被叫方接受或拒接；拒接可携带结构化响应（消息、回拨提醒、语音信箱）。在实时通话期间收到第二个来电会强制进行显式选择：结束并接听、保持并接听，或拒接。

### 通话会被记录

已完成、未接和拒接的通话会在通话记录中留下条目。记录对用户可见且可操作（回拨），在成熟产品中它是可过滤的（全部 / 未接 / 未知主叫）。

### 身份门控可触达性

用户通常只能呼叫存在于服务身份空间中的人员（他们的联系人或服务的用户群）。这使得人员界面既是用户体验界面，也是访问边界。产品在处理陌生人方面有所不同——一些过滤或静音未知主叫，一些允许阻止。

### 视频是同一通话，而非不同对象

视频通话共享音频通话的身份、记录条目和生命周期；它可以作为音频接听，音频通话也可以升级。将视频作为默认模式的产品正在向视频通话应用类型漂移，但底层通话对象是相同的。

### 突破通话在存在时按量计费

呼叫普通固定电话或移动号码，在提供时，是服务的付费层（额度、订阅或入站号码），区别于定义该类型的免费人员到人员通话。

definition.name: Video Calling Application
definition.overview:
A **Video Calling Application** is a person-addressed live video conversation tool: the user places a call to a specific person — picked from a personal reachability surface such as a contact list, or addressed directly by phone number, email, or username — the recipient answers, and the participants see and hear each other in real time until they hang up.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Personal reachability surface
└── Call placed to a specific person (answered, not joined)
    └── Live real-time audiovisual connection (video as the medium)
        └── Bounded call lifecycle (ringing → connected → ended)
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern video calling — contact lists, group calls, call history, visual effects, shareable links, recording — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. Older videophone-era products (a call dialed to a phone number over the mobile network) and desktop-era videochat products (a call placed to a username) satisfy the same definition without any of the modern specifics.

When the organizing object shifts to a convened meeting that participants join by address, the product is a Video Conferencing Application; when a persistent personal social space becomes the center, it is a Live Video Chat Application; when the platform assigns the counterpart, it is Random Video Chat.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**视频通话应用**是一种面向特定个人的实时视频对话工具：用户向特定个人发起呼叫——该个人可从个人可达性界面（如联系人列表）中选取，或通过电话号码、电子邮件或用户名直接指定——接收方接听后，参与者可实时互见互听，直至挂断。

其定义性结构十分简洁：

```text
个人可达性界面
└── 向特定个人发起呼叫（需接听，而非加入）
     └── 实时音视频连接（以视频为媒介）
         └── 有边界的呼叫生命周期（响铃 → 接通 → 结束）
```

现代视频通话中常见的其他功能——联系人列表、群组通话、通话记录、视觉特效、可分享链接、录音——虽在当前产品中普遍存在，但并非定义性核心的一部分。早期的可视电话时代产品（通过移动网络向电话号码拨号）和桌面时代视频聊天产品（向用户名发起呼叫）均满足相同定义，无需具备任何现代特定功能。

当组织对象转变为参与者通过地址加入的召集会议时，该产品即为视频会议应用；当持久性个人社交空间成为中心时，即为实时视频聊天应用；当平台分配对话对象时，即为随机视频聊天。
definition.dc:
Three structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a video calling application:

- **The person-addressed call** — the organizing object is the call itself, placed by addressing a specific identified person through a personal reachability surface, and **answered** by the recipient. The counterpart is addressed by the caller — not convened at a meeting address that people join, and not assigned by the platform. This is what makes a call a call: the recipient decides whether to pick up.
- **Live real-time audiovisual connection, with video as the medium of record** — while connected, participants see and hear each other in real time. The product exists to put faces on the conversation; an audio-only mode is a fallback within the product, not its identity. Remove the video and only the call remains — a voice call.
- **The bounded call lifecycle** — the call exists as a discrete session with connection states: placed → ringing → connected → ended, with declined and missed outcomes. It ends when the participants hang up. The product holds no persistent shared space beyond the call. Remove this and the product drifts toward an always-on room or a scheduled convened session.
definition.dc_zh:
三个结构。如果移除任何一个，产品将不再被识别为视频通话应用：

1. **针对个人的呼叫** — 组织对象是呼叫本身，通过个人可寻址界面呼叫特定识别的人，并由接收者应答。接收者由呼叫者寻址——不是通过人们加入的会议地址召集，也不是由平台分配。这正是呼叫的本质：接收者决定是否接听。

2. **实时音视频连接，视频作为记录媒介** — 连接时，参与者实时看到和听到彼此。产品的目的是在对话中显示面孔；仅音频模式是产品内的后备，而不是其身份。移除视频，只剩下呼叫——语音呼叫。

3. **有限的呼叫生命周期** — 呼叫作为离散会话存在，具有连接状态：发起 → 振铃 → 连接 → 结束，有拒绝和未接结果。当参与者挂断时结束。产品在呼叫之外没有持久共享空间。移除这个，产品趋向于始终在线的房间或计划召集的会话。
definition.rules:
- **The recipient decides.** A call is placed at a person, so connecting depends on the recipient answering — not on an open room. Declined and unanswered calls are first-class outcomes, not errors.
- **Calls reach the locked device.** Incoming calls ring even when the application is closed; the calling posture is inherited from telephony, not from a content feed.
- **The call is bounded.** When participants hang up, the session is over. In group calls, the call commonly stays alive for the remaining participants, and some products let a departed participant rejoin from the call history while the call is still active.
- **The reachability surface is also an access boundary.** The user calls people they can address; unknown or unwanted callers can be filtered, silenced, or blocked.
- **No persistent space.** Nothing survives the call except the call record (and, where offered, an explicit recording the participants chose to make). This is the structural contrast with rooms, offices, and meeting workspaces.
definition.rules_zh:
- **由接收方决定。** 呼叫指向个人，因此连接取决于接收方接听——而非开放房间。被拒绝和未接来电是一等结果，而非错误。
- **呼叫可达锁定设备。** 即使应用关闭，来电仍会响铃；呼叫姿态继承自电信，而非内容信息流。
- **呼叫有边界。** 参与者挂断时，会话结束。在群组通话中，通话通常对剩余参与者保持活跃，部分产品允许已离开参与者在通话仍活跃时从通话历史重新加入。
- **可达性界面也是访问边界。** 用户呼叫其可寻址的人员；未知或不受欢迎的来电者可被过滤、静音或拦截。
- **无持久空间。** 除通话记录（及在提供时参与者选择制作的明确录音）外，无内容在通话后存续。这是与房间、办公室和会议工作空间的结构性对比。

definition.name: Social Profile Network
definition.overview:
A **Social Profile Network** is an application whose primary object is the **personal profile of record**: a persistent, self-maintained profile bound to one person, addressable in a shared namespace, and designed to be consumed outside the application itself — embedded in other sites, linked from other platforms, shared person-to-person, or synced into other systems.

It solves a problem every other social application treats as incidental: a person's identity scattered across many surfaces, each holding a stale copy. Here the profile is the whole product. The user maintains one authoritative record of themselves; the application's job is to make that record findable, trustworthy, and consumable everywhere it is referenced.

The defining core is deliberately narrow. A content feed, a follower graph, messaging, and audience analytics are all common in some products of this family, but none of them defines it. What defines it is the profile as a portable, addressable identity object whose primary consumption happens elsewhere.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**社交档案网络**是一种应用程序，其核心对象是**个人档案记录**：一个持久的、由用户自行维护的档案，绑定于特定个人，可在共享命名空间中寻址，并设计为在应用程序外部被消费——嵌入其他网站、从其他平台链接、在人与人之间共享，或同步到其他系统中。

它解决了一个其他所有社交应用都视为附带问题的问题：一个人的身份分散在许多表面上，每个表面都持有一份过时的副本。在这里，档案就是整个产品。用户维护一份关于自己的权威记录；应用程序的工作是让该记录在引用它的任何地方都可被发现、可信赖且可被消费。

其定义性核心被刻意保持狭窄。内容信息流、关注图谱、消息传递和受众分析在该家族的部分产品中很常见，但没有任何一项能定义它。定义它的是档案作为一个可移植的、可寻址的身份对象，其主要消费发生在别处。
definition.dc:
```text
Personal Profile of Record
└── Shared-namespace addressability
    └── Outward consumption design
```

Three structures, jointly held:

- **Personal profile of record** — a persistent profile bound to one person, owned and maintained by that person (or, in organization-facing variants, issued to them and claimed by them). It accumulates the person's identity content over time and survives any single use. Without it, the product is just an identity-assertion service.
- **Shared-namespace addressability** — the profile carries a stable identifier in a namespace shared across the whole user population: a unique iD, a handle, a username URL, a hash-keyed address. Other people *and other systems* use this identifier to find and reference the profile. Without it, the profile is a private account page — a capability of any product, not a Type.
- **Outward consumption design** — the profile is built to leave the application: fetched by other systems through public interfaces, linked from other platforms, exchanged person-to-person, embedded in third-party contexts. The product's value is the profile's circulation, not time spent inside it. Without this, the product is merely another application's internal profile page.
definition.dc_zh:
官方个人档案
└── 共享命名空间的可寻址性
    └── 向外消费设计
definition.rules:
- **The profile is the record; copies derive from it.** Wherever the profile is consumed — an embedded avatar, an exchanged card, a third-party fetch — the application-side record is authoritative. Linked copies update when the record changes; this "self-updating copy" behavior is the family's signature promise.
- **Addressability is stable.** The namespace identifier is designed to persist across role, employer, and platform changes — that stability is precisely what other systems build on.
- **Visibility is field-level.** Profiles mix public and private content; mature products give the owner per-field control over what the namespace exposes.
- **Self-authored, optionally verified.** The profile's content is the owner's own assertion. Verification features (verified accounts, institutional links) attach external trust to selected fields but do not replace self-authorship.
- **No feed obligation.** Nothing in the core model requires a content stream. Products that add one treat it as an extension; when the stream becomes the primary consumption surface, the product has drifted toward a feed-centered social network Type.
definition.rules_zh:
- **档案是记录；副本源自它。** 无论档案在哪里被消费——嵌入的头像、交换的名片、第三方获取——应用程序端的记录是权威的。当记录更改时，链接的副本会更新；这种“自更新副本”行为是该家族的标志性承诺。
- **可寻址性是稳定的。** 命名空间标识符被设计为在角色、雇主和平台变更中持久存在——这种稳定性正是其他系统所构建的基础。
- **可见性是字段级的。** 档案混合了公共和私有内容；成熟的产品为所有者提供对命名空间暴露内容的逐字段控制。
- **自撰，可选验证。** 档案的内容是所有者自己的断言。验证功能（已验证账户、机构链接）将外部信任附加到选定字段，但不取代自撰性。
- **无信息流义务。** 核心模型中没有任何内容要求内容流。添加信息流的产品将其视为扩展；当流成为主要消费表面时，该产品已偏离向以信息流为中心的社交网络类型。

definition.name: Live Video Chat Application
definition.overview:
A **Live Video Chat Application** is a social application whose center is the live, real-time, two-way video conversation: equal participants meet on camera in one-to-one or small-group conversations, each conversation is with counterparts the user has chosen, and the product holds a persistent personal social context — a profile, relationships, messaging, and a record of past conversations — around those live conversations.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Live two-way video conversation (everyone on camera, live while it happens)
└── Equal peers in a small co-present group (no broadcaster, no audience)
    └── User-selected counterparts (relationships, suggestions, or a browsable pool — never random assignment)
        └── Persistent personal social context (profile · relationships · messaging · history)
```

Everything commonly associated with the category — browsing who is online, in-call games and effects, virtual currencies and subscriptions, kids and family editions, large group calls — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product one of this kind. A bare application for live video conversations with chosen people, wrapped in nothing but a profile and a history, still fits the definition completely.

The removals that make the Type recognizable: remove the *personal social context* and the product becomes a pure video-calling utility; remove *user selection* — let the platform draw the counterpart at random — and it becomes random video chat; give one side the floor and the other side an audience, and it becomes live streaming; switch the medium to a governed audio floor, and it becomes social audio.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**实时视频聊天应用**是一种以实时、双向视频对话为核心的社交应用：地位平等的参与者通过摄像头进行一对一或小型群体的对话，每次对话的对象都是用户自行选择的，并且产品在这些实时对话周围维持着一个持久的个人社交语境——包括个人资料、关系网络、消息记录以及过往对话的历史记录。

其定义性结构非常精简：

```text
实时双向视频对话（所有人开启摄像头，实时进行）
└── 小型共在群体中的平等对等者（无主播，无观众）
     └── 用户选择的对话对象（基于关系、推荐或可浏览的池子——绝非随机分配）
         └── 持久的个人社交语境（个人资料 · 关系 · 消息 · 历史）
```

通常与该类别相关联的一切——浏览谁在线、通话中的游戏和特效、虚拟货币和订阅服务、儿童及家庭版、大型群组通话——虽然在当前产品中普遍存在，但这并非使产品属于此类型的本质特征。一个仅用于与选定人员进行实时视频对话的极简应用，仅包裹着个人资料和历史记录，也完全符合该定义。

使该类型可识别的移除操作如下：移除*个人社交语境*，产品就变成了纯粹的视频通话工具；移除*用户选择*——让平台随机分配对话对象——它就变成了随机视频聊天；赋予一方发言权而另一方成为观众，它就变成了直播；将媒介切换为受管理的音频发言权，它就变成了社交音频。
definition.dc: - **The persistent personal social context.** The product holds a profile, relationships, and messaging/history around the live conversations, so that a conversation is one surface of an ongoing personal social space: people you met stay reachable, past conversations leave a trace you can act on, and your identity accumulates. Remove this and the product is a pure video-calling utility — a different Type (Video Calling Application).
definition.dc_zh: - **持久的个人社交上下文。** 产品围绕实时对话保存个人资料、关系和消息/历史记录，使得对话成为持续个人社交空间的一个表面：你认识的人保持可达，过去的对话留下可操作的痕迹，你的身份得以积累。移除这一点，产品就是一个纯粹的视频通话工具——一个不同的类型（视频通话应用）。
definition.rules:
- **Both sides are on camera.** The conversation is two-way video by default; camera and microphone are personal toggles. This symmetric exposure is what distinguishes the Type from broadcast forms, where appearing is a granted role.
- **Selection belongs to the user.** Products may narrow the pool (preferences, filters) and may gate a connection on availability, but the counterpart is never randomly assigned. Where a product does assign counterparts randomly, it has become a different Type.
- **Encounters persist as relationships.** The follow/add-from-history mechanic converts live conversations into standing connections. What persists is the social trace — profile, relationship, messages, history — not the video itself; live conversations are live-first and leave no replay unless the product explicitly records them.
- **Conduct rules attach to the camera.** Where strangers meet, published rules (what may be shown and said), in-conversation reporting, and account enforcement are structural parts of the product, not optional extras.
- **Monetization wraps the conversation.** Where products charge, the core conversation remains the free center in the researched market, with payment attached around it — subscription tiers, virtual currencies, paid filters and messages. Postures vary; the free core is the norm but not an invariant.
- **Group scale is a product decision.** Group conversations are common; their size limits vary substantially by product and are not part of the Type's definition.
definition.rules_zh:
- **双方都在摄像头前。** 对话默认是双向视频；摄像头和麦克风是个人开关。这种对称的暴露是该类型与广播形式的区别所在，在广播形式中，出镜是一种被授予的角色。
- **选择权属于用户。** 产品可以缩小池子（偏好、过滤器）并可以将连接建立在可用性之上，但对话对象绝非随机分配。如果产品随机分配对话对象，它就变成了另一种类型。
- **相遇持久化为关系。** 从历史中关注/添加的机制将实时对话转化为固定的连接。持久存在的是社交痕迹——个人资料、关系、消息、历史——而非视频本身；实时对话以实时为先，除非产品明确记录，否则不留回放。
- **行为准则附着于摄像头。** 在陌生人相遇的地方，已发布的规则（允许展示和说什么）、对话中的举报以及账户执行是产品的结构性部分，而非可选附加项。
- **变现包裹着对话。** 在产品收费的地方，核心对话在研究市场中仍保持免费中心地位，付费附着在其周围——订阅层级、虚拟货币、付费过滤器和消息。姿态各异；免费核心是常态但非不变量。
- **群组规模是产品决策。** 群组对话很常见；其大小限制因产品而异且差异巨大，不属于该类型的定义部分。

definition.name: PDF / Document Reader
definition.overview:
A **PDF / Document Reader** is an application for reading document files produced elsewhere: it opens a whole document — regardless of subject matter or origin — renders its pages faithfully in the layout the file defines, and lets the reader move through the document and interact with its content without changing what the document *is*.

The defining core is small:

```text
Document file from an external source
└── Faithful fixed-layout page rendering
    └── Movement through the paginated document
        (paging, jumping, scale adjustment)
```

Everything else commonly associated with PDF applications — annotation, form filling, digital signatures, text search, page reorganization, enterprise security tooling, AI assistance — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a document reader. The Type's historical root is the plain read-only viewer, and a viewer with none of the modern machinery remains fully inside the Type.

When the center of gravity shifts — re-laying-out content for reading comfort, authoring or editing the document's content, curating a collection of books or papers — the product has drifted toward a different Application Type (E-book Reader, Document Editor, E-book Library, Academic Paper Reader).
definition.overview_zh:
一款 **PDF / 文档阅读器** 是用于阅读在其他地方生成的文档文件的应用程序：它打开整个文档——无论主题或来源如何——按照文件定义的布局忠实地渲染其页面，并允许读者在文档中移动并与内容交互，而不改变文档*本身*的性质。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
来自外部源的文档文件
└── 忠实的固定布局页面渲染
     └── 在分页文档中的移动
         （翻页、跳转、缩放调整）
```

通常与 PDF 应用程序相关联的其他一切——注释、表单填写、数字签名、文本搜索、页面重组、企业安全工具、AI 辅助——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使该产品成为文档阅读器的原因。该类型的历史根源是纯只读查看器，一个没有现代机制的查看器仍然完全属于该类型。

当重心转移——为阅读舒适度重新布局内容、创作或编辑文档内容、整理书籍或论文集合——该产品已偏离到不同的应用程序类型（电子书阅读器、文档编辑器、电子书库、学术论文阅读器）。
definition.dc:
```text
Document file from an external source
└── Faithful fixed-layout page rendering
    └── Movement through the paginated document
        (paging, jumping, scale adjustment)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a document reader:

- **The externally-obtained document as the unit of reading.** The application opens whole document files of arbitrary provenance and content — invoices, manuals, papers, forms, brochures. It holds no authoring relationship to the content and no collection semantics of its own. Without this, the product is an authoring tool or a content service, not a reader.
- **Faithful fixed-layout page rendering.** Pages are presented as fixed compositions — text, images, and graphics placed at exact positions, with pagination determined by the file itself. The same file looks the same everywhere; the application's obligation is fidelity to the file as authored, not re-presentation for comfort. Without this, the product re-lays-out content (e-book reader) or changes content (editor).
- **Movement through the paginated document.** Because the layout is fixed and does not adapt to the window, reading requires machinery to move: scrolling and paging between pages, jumping to a page or position, and adjusting viewing scale (zoom, fit-to-window/page/width). Without this, the product is a static page image.
definition.dc_zh:
来自外部源的文档文件
└── 忠实的固定布局页面渲染
    └── 在分页文档中移动
        (翻页、跳转、缩放调整)
definition.rules:
### Fidelity is the obligation

The reader renders what the file says. It does not re-flow text to fit the window, does not re-typeface for comfort, does not "improve" the layout. Everything that changes presentation rather than scale belongs to other Types. This is the structural contrast with e-book reading, where the presentation is the app's to optimize.

### The text layer is not guaranteed

A PDF's pages may be true text or may be scanned images. When there is no text layer, search, selection, and copy do not work — a failure mode documented in mainstream products' own troubleshooting guides. Text recognition features in some products exist precisely to bridge this gap; the base behavior is: **no text layer, no text interaction**.

### Documents carry permissions; readers enforce them

An author can protect a document: a password to open it, and restrictions on printing or copying content. The reader enforces these — it can refuse to print a restricted document or require a password before text can be copied. The reader never grants rights the file does not carry.

### Markup and form data are changes to a copy

Annotation and form input modify the opened document (or a copy of it). Persistence mechanics differ — some products write back into the file, some require an explicit save-as-copy step — but in all cases unsaved work is transient. A filled form that is not saved is lost.

### The outline is the document's, not the app's

A table of contents exists only if the authoring tool put one in the file. Most documents carry none; the reader must remain fully usable through thumbnails, page numbers, and search alone.

### The file is live

The reader views a file that other programs may change while it is open; products commonly reload the document when the file changes underneath. The reader is a window onto the file, not a container that owns it.

### Reading is not editing

The line the market itself maintains: readers present, mark up, fill, and sign; they do not rewrite the document's content. Products that do both split the capability into a separate editor product or explicitly disclaim editing. Page-level organization (combining, reordering, deleting pages) is the gray zone — offered by some readers as a convenience, owned by editors as a job — and is treated here as optional, never defining.
definition.rules_zh:
### 保真度是义务

阅读器渲染文件所说的内容。它不重新流动文本以适应窗口，不为舒适度重新排版，不“改进”布局。所有改变呈现而非比例的内容属于其他类型。这与电子书阅读形成结构性对比，在电子书阅读中，呈现是应用程序要优化的。

### 文本层不是保证的

PDF 的页面可能是真正的文本，也可能是扫描图像。当没有文本层时，搜索、选择和复制不起作用——这是主流产品自己的故障排除指南中记录的故障模式。某些产品中的文本识别功能正是为了弥合这一差距；基本行为是：**没有文本层，就没有文本交互**。

### 文档携带权限；阅读器执行它们

作者可以保护文档：打开它的密码，以及对打印或复制内容的限制。阅读器执行这些——它可以拒绝打印受限制的文档，或在复制文本前要求密码。阅读器从不授予文件不携带的权利。

### 标记和表单数据是对副本的更改

注释和表单输入修改打开的文档（或其副本）。持久化机制不同——一些产品写回文件，一些需要显式的另存为副本步骤——但在所有情况下，未保存的工作是暂时的。未保存的已填写表单会丢失。

### 大纲属于文档，不属于应用程序

只有当创作工具在文件中放入目录时，目录才存在。大多数文档没有；阅读器必须仅通过缩略图、页码和搜索保持完全可用。

### 文件是活动的

阅读器查看的文件可能在打开时被其他程序更改；产品通常在文件更改时重新加载文档

definition.name: Public Data Portal
definition.overview:
A **Public Data Portal** is a publication platform through which an organization makes collections of data available to the general public as **datasets** — each held as a persistent, metadata-described record to which the data itself is attached as downloadable files or queryable APIs. The public discovers data through an open catalog (search and browse), evaluates each dataset from its record (what it contains, who published it, what it covers, how current it is, how it may be used), and takes the data away for its own purposes.

The defining core is small:

```text
Maintained dataset record (metadata-described, the portal's own catalog content)
└── Data distributions (files and/or APIs attached to the record)
    └── Public discovery surface (open search/browse over the whole corpus)
        └── Public-access posture (published once for all comers, under recorded terms)
```

Everything commonly associated with modern portals — in-browser charts and maps, query APIs with developer documentation, publisher workspaces, update automation, usage analytics — is widespread in current products but is not what makes a portal a portal. Simple table-first statistical services, early-generation catalogs, and small single-publisher download sites satisfy the same definition. The operator can be any body — a government (the specialized case documented separately), an international organization, a statistical agency, a research institution, or an open community.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**公共数据门户**是一个发布平台，组织通过它向公众提供数据集合，作为**数据集**——每个数据集都作为一条持久且带有元数据描述的记录保存，数据本身以可下载文件或可查询 API 的形式附着于该记录。公众通过开放目录（搜索与浏览）发现数据，根据记录评估每个数据集（其包含内容、发布者、覆盖范围、时效性、使用方式），并将数据取走用于自身目的。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
维护的数据集记录（带元数据描述，属于门户自身的目录内容）
└── 数据分发形式（附着于记录的文件和/或 API）
     └── 公共发现界面（覆盖整个语料的开放搜索/浏览）
         └── 公共访问姿态（面向所有来者一次性发布，遵循已记录的条件）
```

现代门户通常关联的一切——浏览器内图表与地图、带开发者文档的查询 API、发布者工作区、更新自动化、使用分析——在当前产品中虽已普及，但并非使门户成为门户的本质。简单的表格优先统计服务、早期目录以及小型单发布者下载站点同样满足此定义。运营方可以是任何机构——政府（作为单独记录的特例）、国际组织、统计机构、研究机构或开放社区。
definition.dc:
- **The public discovery surface.** A search and browse layer over the whole corpus — free-text search, browse listings by topic, publisher, geography, or format — open to anyone, with no need to know in advance which organization holds what and, in the typical case, no account required. Without this, the product is an internal records tool or a private data service.
- **The public-access posture.** The corpus is published **once, for all comers**: acquiring data is governed by the usage terms or license recorded on or alongside the dataset, not by per-consumer grants, subscriptions, or entitlement decisions. Reuse conditions ride with the data; admission to the corpus does not depend on who is asking. Without this, the product drifts toward subscription data services and data-exchange territory.
definition.dc_zh:
- **公共发现界面。** 一个搜索和浏览层，覆盖整个语料库——支持自由文本搜索，按主题、发布者、地理位置或格式浏览列表——对任何人开放，无需事先知道哪个组织持有什么，在典型情况下，无需账户。如果没有这个功能，该产品就是一个内部记录工具或私有数据服务。
- **公共访问姿态。** 语料库**一次性发布，供所有人使用**：获取数据受数据集上或旁边的用法条款或许可证管理，而非针对每个消费者的授权、订阅或权益决定。重用条件随数据而定；进入语料库不取决于谁在请求。如果没有这个特性，产品会倾向于订阅数据服务和数据交换领域。
definition.rules:
- **Published once, for all comers.** There is no requester relationship and no per-consumer entitlement decision. This is the structural line against data-sharing products that mediate access party by party, and against subscription statistics services.
- **Records are maintained, not crawled.** The catalog's entries are the operator's own curated content — even when aggregated from many sources. A service that only indexes third-party data pages is a search engine, not a portal.
- **Terms ride with the data.** Usage conditions are recorded on the dataset or alongside it; their granularity varies (per-record licenses, site-level conditions, per-dataset terms), but the consumer can always see what reuse allows before acquiring.
- **Freshness is declared, not guaranteed.** Update dates and frequencies are metadata; whether a dataset is mechanically refreshed or manually updated varies by dataset and by operator.
- **The portal delivers; it does not own the data of record.** Published datasets are copies, exports, or live views of data whose authoritative versions live in source systems — statistical systems, administrative registers, survey programs.
- **Anonymous by default.** Discovery and download typically require no account; accounts exist for publishing and engagement, not for admission to the corpus.
definition.rules_zh:
- **一次性发布，面向所有来者。** 不存在请求者关系，也不存在针对每个消费者的授权决策。这是与逐方中介访问的数据共享产品以及订阅制统计服务之间的结构性分界线。
- **记录是维护的，而非爬取的。** 目录条目是运营方自身策划的内容——即使是从多个来源聚合而来。仅索引第三方数据页面的服务是搜索引擎，而非门户。
- **条款随数据同行。** 使用条件记录在数据集上或其旁侧；其粒度各异（逐记录许可、站点级条件、逐数据集条款），但消费者在获取前总能看清允许何种复用。
- **时效性是被声明的，而非被保证的。** 更新日期与频率属于元数据；数据集是机械刷新还是手动更新，因数据集与运营方而异。
- **门户负责交付，但不拥有权威数据。** 已发布的数据集是副本、导出或实时视图，其权威版本存在于源系统中——统计系统、行政登记册、调查项目。
- **默认匿名。** 发现与下载通常无需账户；账户用于发布与互动，而非用于进入语料库的准入。

definition.name: Reading Library Application
definition.overview:
A **Reading Library Application** maintains a person's own library of book records: persistent entries for books the person has read, is reading, wants to read, or owns, organized on shelves or collections the person controls, with each record carrying that reader's relationship to the book — reading state, dates and progress, ownership, ratings, reviews, notes.

The defining core is small:

```text
Book record (bibliographic identity)
└── held in the person's own organized, retained library
    └── carrying that reader's personal relationship to the book
```

What it does **not** hold is the books themselves. A reading library keeps records *about* books — the actual reading happens elsewhere: a physical copy, an e-reader, an audiobook app, a borrowed library book. If the product holds book content and presents it for reading, it has drifted into E-book Library territory; if its entries are links to web pages held for later consumption, it is a Read-it-later or Bookmark Manager.

The type appears in the market under two dominant shapes — the **reading tracker** (organized by reading status: want to read, currently reading, read, did not finish) and the **private library catalog** (organized by possession: what is on my shelves) — both built on the same core.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**阅读图书馆应用**维护个人专属的图书记录库：包含已读、在读、想读或拥有的书籍的持久化条目，这些条目被组织在由用户自行管理的书架或收藏集中，每条记录都承载着读者与该书的关系——阅读状态、日期与进度、所有权、评分、书评、笔记。

其定义性核心非常精简：

```text
图书记录（书目身份）
└── 存放于个人自行组织并保留的图书馆中
     └── 承载该读者与书籍的个人关系
```

它**不**存储书籍本身。阅读图书馆保存的是*关于*书籍的记录——实际阅读发生在别处：实体书、电子阅读器、有声书应用或借阅的图书馆书籍。如果产品存储书籍内容并供阅读，则已偏离至电子图书馆领域；如果其条目是供日后消费的网页链接，则属于稍后阅读或书签管理器。

该类型在市场上呈现两种主导形态——**阅读追踪器**（按阅读状态组织：想读、在读、已读、未完成）和**私人图书馆目录**（按拥有情况组织：书架上有什么）——两者均建立在相同的核心之上。
definition.dc_zh:
**书籍记录。** 单元是所有事物的持久、个体识别的书籍记录——锚定于书目身份：至少标题和作者，通常包括封面图像、版本、出版细节和描述。记录由个人主动添加：通过搜索产品图书目录、导入从另一服务导出的文件、扫描ISBN条码或手动创建条目。记录是被保留的；它既不是网页链接，也不是书籍文件。

**个人图书馆。** 记录存在于个人自己的图书馆中——一个可搜索和浏览的整体，组织成用户管理的组。规范组是*书架*或*收藏集*：个人控制的命名集合。图书馆被保留，而非消耗——已读的书籍保留在记录中，通常终身。这是待读队列的结构对立面，后者会清除已处理项目。

**个人关系层。** 将书籍目录变成*我的*图书馆的是记录读者与每本书关系的数据层。这一层是个人层，不是固定清单——产品以不同方式组合它，借鉴于：- **阅读状态** — 书籍在阅读生活中的位置：想读 / 正在阅读 / 已读，通常还有未完成或停止状态；- **阅读日期和进度** — 书籍被阅读的时间。
definition.rules:
- **Records, not content.** The product never presents the text of the book. Every object in the system is about the book (identity, status, opinion); the reading itself is done elsewhere. This is the type's clearest structural signature.
- **Retention is normal.** Finished books are not cleared; they accumulate. The library's health is measured by its completeness and growth, not by an empty queue.
- **Status is usually exclusive.** In tracker-form products a book typically occupies exactly one reading status at a time — moving forward moves it out of the previous shelf — while custom shelves/collections hold books independently of status. (Documented explicitly in the sampled open-source tracker; treat the exact mechanics as product-dependent.)
- **One shared identity per book.** Because records resolve against a shared catalog, two readers referencing the same book are referencing the same record — which is what makes community reviews and comparisons possible. Users can usually correct catalog data; some products route corrections to staff review.
- **The library is portable.** Export/import is an expected property; the person's library is their data, movable between products (with the caveat that matching old records to a new catalog is approximate).
- **Privacy is graduated.** A library can be entirely private, per-shelf visible, or public; products differ in the default.
definition.rules_zh:
- **记录，而非内容。** 产品从不呈现书籍文本。系统中的每个对象都是关于书籍的（身份、状态、观点）；阅读本身在别处进行。这是该类型最清晰的结构特征。
- **保留是常态。** 已完成的书籍不会被清除；它们会积累。图书馆的健康度由其完整性和增长衡量，而非空队列。
- **状态通常互斥。** 在追踪器形态产品中，一本书通常一次只占据一个阅读状态——向前移动会将其移出前一个书架——而自定义书架/收藏集独立于状态持有书籍。（在采样的开源追踪器中明确记录；具体机制视产品而定。）
- **每本书一个共享身份。** 因为记录针对共享目录解析，两个读者引用同一本书即引用同一条记录——这正是社区书评和比较成为可能的原因。用户通常可以更正目录数据；部分产品将更正路由至员工审核。
- **图书馆是可移植的。** 导入/导出是预期属性；个人图书馆是其数据，可在产品间移动（但需注意将旧记录匹配到新目录是近似的）。
- **隐私是分级化的。** 图书馆可以完全私密、按书架可见或公开；产品在默认设置上存在差异。

definition.name: Distraction-free Writing Application
definition.overview:
A **Distraction-free Writing Application** is a prose-drafting application built around one promise: while you write, nothing else competes for your attention. Its defining core is small:

```text
Persistent text document
└── Composition surface that presents (nearly) nothing but the text
    └── Drafting as the primary job — formatting and organization deliberately deferred
```

The product's own tools are hidden, minimized, or summoned only on demand; the writing surface occupies the screen (most often full-screen) so that other applications and other tasks recede from view. Formatting is pushed out of the drafting moment — rendered later, or exported into styled output at the end.

This is what separates the Type from a word processor that happens to have a full-screen mode. The attention-preserving surface is not an auxiliary feature here; it is the product's center of gravity, and the rest of the application is arranged around it.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**无干扰写作应用**是一种以散文起草为核心的应用程序，其建立在唯一承诺之上：在你写作时，没有其他事物争夺你的注意力。其定义性核心很小：

```text
持久化文本文档
└── 呈现（几乎）只有文本的写作界面
     └── 起草作为首要任务——格式化和组织被刻意延后
```

产品自身的工具被隐藏、最小化，或仅在按需时召唤；写作界面占据屏幕（通常全屏），使其他应用程序和其他任务从视野中退后。格式化被推离起草时刻——稍后渲染，或在最后导出为样式化输出。

这正是该类型与恰好具有全屏模式的文字处理器的区别所在。在此处，保持注意力的界面不是辅助功能；它是产品的重心，应用程序的其余部分都围绕它安排。
definition.dc:
Three properties. Remove any one and the product stops being recognizable as this Type:

- **Persistent text document** — the writing exists as a durable document that survives sessions. The user returns to the same text across days or months. Without persistence, the product is a scratchpad, not a writing tool.
- **Distraction-free composition surface** — the interface presents (nearly) nothing but the text. In-application tools recede: menus, sidebars, and formatting controls are hidden behind intentional gestures (mouse to the screen edge, a keystroke, a mode switch), and the surface itself takes over the screen so other applications are out of sight. This is where the product's central promise becomes operational.
- **Drafting primacy** — the primary job is producing new prose by continuous text entry. Formatting, structuring, and document management are deliberately subordinated: deferred to separate modes, separate views, or export time. Without this, the product is simply a word processor with a full-screen toggle.
definition.dc_zh: 三个属性。移除任何一个，产品就不再能被识别为此类型：持久文本文档 — 写作以持久文档形式存在，跨越会话。用户在多天或数月内返回同一文本。没有持久性，产品就是草稿本，而不是写作工具。无干扰写作表面 — 界面几乎只呈现文本。应用程序工具退居幕后：菜单、侧边栏和格式化控件隐藏在有意手势后（鼠标移到屏幕边缘、按键、模式切换），表面本身占据屏幕，使其他应用程序不可见。这是产品核心承诺操作化的地方。草稿优先 — 主要工作是通过连续文本输入产生新散文。格式化、结构化和文档管理被有意地置于次要地位：推迟到单独模式、单独视图或导出时间。没有这个，产品就只是一个带全屏切换的字处理软件。
definition.rules:
### The interface hides by design

The distraction-free surface is not a screen mode among many; it is the default state. Tools reappear only through deliberate gestures (moving the mouse to a screen edge, pressing a shortcut, switching views) and disappear again during writing. Applications that merely offer a full-screen toggle inside a permanently chrome-heavy interface do not behave this way.

### Focus mechanics belong to drafting, not editing

Products that dim surrounding text or keep the cursor centered explicitly frame these modes for the writing phase. During revision — selecting, rearranging, cutting — the same mechanics actively interfere (a centered cursor makes selection jump), and the products themselves recommend switching them off. The Type thus encodes a phased workflow: drafting and editing are separated, and the interface changes between them.

### Formatting is deferred, not absent

Deferring formatting does not mean the output is unformatted. The text carries enough structure (headings, emphasis, usually via lightweight markup) for the application to render fully styled output later. What is absent is the *live* formatting decision during drafting.

### Feedback is passive

Statistics and goals report progress; they do not block, nag, or reward. This passivity is what distinguishes drafting feedback inside a writing application from a standalone focus/productivity tool.

### One text in focus, not one document only

Some products keep multiple documents open simultaneously; the defining property is that one text holds the writer's attention and the interface asserts it — other documents, other applications, and other tasks stay out of view.
definition.rules_zh:
### 界面按设计隐藏

无干扰界面不是众多屏幕模式之一；它是默认状态。工具仅通过刻意手势（将鼠标移至屏幕边缘、按下快捷键、切换视图）重新出现，并在写作期间再次消失。仅在永久重界面中提供全屏切换的应用程序并不这样运作。

### 专注机制属于起草，而非编辑

淡化周围文本或保持光标居中的产品明确将这些模式框定为写作阶段。在修订期间——选择、重新排列、剪切——相同机制会主动干扰（居中的光标会使选择跳跃），产品本身建议关闭它们。因此，该类型编码了分阶段工作流：起草和编辑被分离，界面在它们之间变化。

### 格式化被延后，而非缺失

延后格式化并不意味着输出未格式化。文本携带足够的结构（标题、强调，通常通过轻量级标记），以便应用程序稍后渲染完全样式化的输出。缺失的是起草期间的*实时*格式化决策。

### 反馈是被动的

统计和目标报告进度；它们不阻塞、不唠叨、不奖励。这种被动性是将写作应用内的起草反馈与独立专注/生产力工具区分开来的特征。

### 聚焦一个文本，而非仅一个文档

某些产品同时保持多个文档打开；定义性属性是一个文本保持作者的注意力，界面断言这一点——其他文档、其他应用程序和其他任务保持在视野之外。

definition.name: Diagramming Application
definition.overview:
A **Diagramming Application** is an editor for constructing structured visual diagrams — flowcharts, organization charts, network and architecture diagrams, process models, entity-relationship diagrams, floor plans — out of **shapes** drawn from an application-supplied notation vocabulary and joined by **connectors** that stay attached to the shapes they link and re-route as the layout changes.

The defining core is small:

```text
Diagram document (persistent, page-oriented)
└── Shapes — discrete semantic objects placed on the canvas
    └── Connectors — bound to shapes, maintained on move, routed as edges
        └── Application-supplied diagram shape vocabulary (libraries / stencils)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — template galleries, styling, multi-page documents, layers, swimlanes, auto-layout, export and publishing, real-time collaboration, data-linked diagram generation, diagram-as-code — is standard or optional capability layered on that core. Older desktop products from the stencil-and-glue era satisfy the same core as today's cloud products; real-time collaboration, cloud storage, and AI are not what make a product a diagramming application.

The category's sharpest boundary is against the digital whiteboard / collaborative canvas family: vendors themselves police it by shipping diagramming and whiteboarding as separate products, importing each family's files through separate flows, and assigning freehand drawing to the whiteboard side.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**图表绘制应用**是一种用于构建结构化视觉图表的编辑器——包括流程图、组织架构图、网络与架构图、流程模型、实体关系图、平面图——这些图表由从应用提供的符号词汇表中选取的**形状**构成，并通过**连接线**连接；这些连接线始终附着于其所连接的形状，并随布局变化而重新路由。

其定义性核心非常精简：

```text
图表文档（持久化、面向页面）
└── 形状——放置在画布上的离散语义对象
     └── 连接线——绑定于形状，在移动时维护，作为边进行路由
         └── 应用提供的图表形状词汇表（库 / 模板）
```

通常与该类别相关联的其他一切——模板库、样式、多页文档、图层、泳道、自动布局、导出与发布、实时协作、数据链接图表生成、图表即代码——都是叠加在该核心之上的标准或可选功能。来自模板与胶水时代的旧版桌面产品与当今的云产品满足相同的核心；实时协作、云存储和 AI 并非使一个产品成为图表绘制应用的决定性因素。

该类别最清晰的边界是与数字白板 / 协作画布家族之间的区分：厂商自身通过分别发布图表绘制和白板产品、通过独立流程导入各自家族的文件、并将自由手绘分配给白板一侧来维护这一边界。
definition.dc:
**Diagram document.** The diagram lives in a persistent, named document — not an ephemeral session surface. A document commonly holds **multiple pages**, so related diagrams (for example, several views of one system) travel together. Documents are stored by the vendor's cloud, the user's own storage, or as local files, depending on the product.

**Shapes.** The unit of content is a discrete, semantic object: a process box, decision diamond, actor, entity, network device, wall segment. Shapes are dragged onto the canvas from a vocabulary, then selected, moved, resized, labeled, and styled individually. In stencil-based products the shape on the canvas is an **instance** of a **master shape** held in the stencil — the original stays in the library, and any number of instances can be placed. Shapes can carry meaning through their form (a diamond means a decision in a flowchart) and through attached data fields (where data linking is offered).

**Connectors.** The unit of relationship is a line bound to shapes rather than drawn freely. Three behaviors define it:

- *Attachment* — a connector ends on a shape (at a specific connection point, or floating along the shape's border), not at a bare canvas coordinate.
- *Maintained connection* — when a shape moves, its connectors move with it and stay attached. This is the single most load-bearing behavior of the category.
- *Routing* — the connector is managed as an edge: it may take the shortest path around shapes, bend at right angles (elbow routing is a common default), follow user-placed waypoints, hop over crossing lines, and carry labels at its middle and ends plus directional endpoints (arrows, notation-specific symbols such as crow's-foot cardinality or UML arrows).

**Shape vocabulary (libraries / stencils).** The application supplies sets of notation-oriented shapes — flowchart symbols, UML, BPMN, entity-relationship, network and cloud-provider icons, floor-plan elements — that the user enables per document. Mature products add searchable libraries, custom shapes (built from imported images, SVG, or vendor stencils), and team-shared libraries with usage permissions.

**Templates.** Documents typically start from a template for a diagram type, which pre-loads the relevant shape vocabulary, page settings, and example structure. In some products a template also carries scale and measurement settings (for floor and site plans) or step-by-step wizards.

**Supporting structures.** Two structural containers appear across the category: **containers/swimlanes** (bands that group shapes by role, phase, or system, with shapes magnetically held inside) and **layers** (stackable planes of content that can be shown, hidden, or locked, including background pages for borders and titles).
definition.dc_zh:
**图表文档。** 图表存在于一个持久的、命名的文档中——而非临时的会话界面。一个文档通常包含**多个页面**，因此相关的图表（例如，一个系统的多个视图）可以一起保存。文档的存储方式取决于产品：可能由供应商的云存储、用户自己的存储或本地文件存储。

**形状。** 内容的单元是一个离散的、语义化的对象：流程框、决策菱形、参与者、实体、网络设备、墙段。形状从一个词汇库中拖放到画布上，然后可以单独选择、移动、调整大小、标记和样式化。在基于模板的产品中，画布上的形状是**模板中主形状**的**实例**——原始形状保留在库中，可以放置任意数量的实例。形状可以通过其形式（例如，菱形在流程图中表示决策）和附加的数据字段（在提供数据链接时）来承载含义。

**连接器。** 关系的单元是绑定到形状的线，而不是自由绘制的。三个行为定义了它：

- *附着* — 连接器结束于一个形状（在特定的连接点，或沿着形状的边界浮动），而不是在裸画布坐标上。
- *保持连接* — 当形状移动时，其连接器随之移动并保持附着。这是该类别中最关键的行为。

definition.rules:
- **Connection maintenance is the default and can be switched off.** Products let users disable automatic line connections so lines can be placed freely; connections made before the switch remain attached. The default-on behavior is what distinguishes the editor from a drawing surface.
- **Floating vs fixed attachment.** A connector end either floats along the target shape's border (taking the shortest route) or locks to a defined connection point. Products expose both, per connector end, and let shapes define custom connection points.
- **Instances outlive their library.** Removing or deleting a shape library does not remove shapes already placed on the canvas; they persist as instances.
- **Text lives on shapes and connectors.** Labels are part of the object: connector labels move with the connector, and text blocks can be repositioned relative to their shape or line.
- **Routing style is a readability decision.** Elbow (right-angle) routing aligned to the grid is a common default; line jumps mark crossings; notation-specific endpoints (arrows, cardinality symbols) carry meaning that readers depend on.
- **Stacking order and layers affect rendering.** Shapes, connectors, and layers have z-order; connectors can be sent behind shapes; background pages hold borders and titles behind every page.
- **Swimlanes hold their contents.** Shapes placed in a lane/container move with it and are magnetically constrained to it.
- **Notation is convention, not enforcement.** A diagramming application draws UML, BPMN, or ER notation faithfully, but — unlike domain-specific modeling tools — it generally does not validate the model's semantics or generate code from it.
- **Data-linked documents can expose their data.** In at least some products, viewers of a data-linked document see the full linked dataset even in view-only mode; sharing such a document shares its data.
- **Scale is opt-in.** Only scale-oriented variants (floor plans, site plans) use real-world measurement; ordinary diagrams are symbolic and not to scale.
definition.rules_zh:
- **连接维护是默认行为，但可以关闭。** 产品允许用户禁用自动线条连接，以便自由放置线条；在切换前建立的连接仍保持附着。默认开启的行为是将该编辑器与绘图表面区分开来的关键。
- **浮动与固定附着。** 连接线端点要么沿目标形状的边界浮动（取最短路径），要么锁定到定义的连接点。产品为每个连接线端点提供这两种模式，并允许形状定义自定义连接点。
- **实例比其库更持久。** 移除或删除形状库不会移除已放置在画布上的形状；它们作为实例持续存在。
- **文本存在于形状和连接线上。** 标签是对象的一部分：连接线标签随连接线移动，文本块可以相对于其形状或线条重新定位。
- **路由样式是可读性决策。** 对齐网格的肘形（直角）路由是常见默认值；线条跳跃标记交叉点；特定符号的端点（箭头、基数符号）承载读者所依赖的含义。
- **堆叠顺序和图层影响渲染。** 形状、连接线和图层具有 z 顺序；连接线可以置于形状之后；背景页面在每个页面之后持有边框和标题。
- **泳道保持其内容。** 放置在泳道/容器中的形状随其移动，并被磁性地约束于其中。
- **符号是约定，而非强制。** 图表绘制应用忠实地绘制 UML、BPMN 或 ER 符号，但——与领域特定的建模工具不同——它通常不验证模型的语义或从中生成代码。

definition.name: To-do List Application
definition.overview:
A **To-do List Application** is a personal application that holds **lists of to-do items** — lightweight records of things the person intends to do — and lets the user capture them, be reminded of them, and **check them off** when done.

The defining structure is small:

```text
To-do item (one thing to do; completable — open → done)
└── held on a list
    └── the list is the primary working surface
        └── derived views (daily focus, smart lists) are lenses over the lists
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern to-do apps — due dates, reminders, recurrence, subtasks, tags, shared lists, smart views, calendar bridges — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a to-do list. A paper list on the refrigerator, with items crossed off by hand, satisfies the same core; the products in this Type digitize it and add the machinery around it.

The posture the Type realizes is **capture-and-remember**: the app's promise is that what you intend to do is held somewhere you will see it, reminded when it matters, and crossed off when finished. When a product's center of gravity shifts to deliberately organizing a population of work and working it through views, it is functioning as a Task Management Application — a sibling Type that shares the same record grammar.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**待办事项列表应用程序**是一种个人应用，用于保存**待办事项列表**——即记录个人打算完成之事的轻量级条目——并允许用户记录这些事项、接收提醒，并在完成后**将其勾选**。

其定义性结构非常小巧：

```text
待办事项（一件要做的事；可完成——从待办 → 已完成）
└── 保存在列表中
     └── 列表是主要的工作界面
         └── 衍生视图（每日重点、智能列表）是列表的透视角度
```

现代待办应用通常关联的其他功能——截止日期、提醒、重复、子任务、标签、共享列表、智能视图、日历桥接——在当前产品中虽已普及，但并非使该产品成为待办列表的本质。冰箱上的一张手写清单，通过手动划掉项目，同样满足这一核心需求；本类型中的产品将其数字化，并围绕其添加了相关机制。

该类型所实现的态度是**捕获与记忆**：应用的承诺是，你打算做的事会被保存在你能够看到的地方，在重要时刻提醒你，并在完成后被划掉。当产品的重心转向有意识地组织一批工作并通过视图进行处理时，它实际上是在作为任务管理应用程序运行——这是一种共享相同记录语法的姊妹类型。
definition.dc:
- **The list as the primary container and working surface.** Items are held on named lists; the list is the surface the user opens, reviews, and works from — capture, review, and completion happen on the list. Views derived from the lists (a daily-focus list, criteria-based smart lists) are lenses: they gather items from the lists, but the items' home remains the list. Without the list as the home and working surface — items managed as a population through organizing structure and views — the product has become a task manager.

The record grammar is deliberately minimal: **open → done**, with urgency (overdue, due today) derived from the item's own date rather than from workflow stages.
definition.dc_zh:
列表作为主要容器和工作表面。项目存储在命名列表中；列表是用户打开、查看和工作的表面——捕获、审查和完成都在列表上进行。从列表派生的视图（如每日焦点列表、基于条件的智能列表）是透镜：它们从列表中收集项目，但项目的归属地仍然是列表。如果没有列表作为归属地和工作表面——项目通过组织结构和视图作为整体管理——该产品已成为任务管理器。

记录语法故意最小化：开放 → 完成，紧急性（逾期、今日到期）从项目自身的日期派生，而非工作流阶段。
definition.rules:
- **Completion is a first-class act, and it is reversible.** Checking off is the defining state change; products keep completed items retrievable (history, or restore from a deleted-items path) because check-offs sometimes happen by mistake.
- **The list is the home of record.** Smart lists and daily views gather items but do not own them; an item edited or completed through a lens changes in its home list. In products with a nightly-resetting daily list, uncompleted items are explicitly returned to their home list rather than lost.
- **Urgency is derived, not staged.** Overdue and due-today states are computed from the item's date attributes; there are no user-defined workflow stages on items. Multi-stage item lifecycles belong to task-management and issue-tracking territory.
- **Recurrence re-materializes the item.** A repeating item's next occurrence appears on completion; the completed occurrences remain as history. Recurrence is an attribute of an item, not a separately managed routine population.
- **Sharing is list-scoped and personal.** Invitees act on the whole list; assignment hands a single item to a person. There is no org-chart role model, no approval step, no permission hierarchy beyond owner/invitee.
- **Reminders are the safety net, not the organizer.** The notification layer (time, location, repeated alerts, overdue notices) exists so that capture-and-remember actually works; it does not reorder or re-plan the lists by itself.
definition.rules_zh:
- **完成是一等动作，且可逆。** 勾选是定义性的状态变更；产品保留已完成条目的可检索性（历史，或从已删除条目路径恢复），因为勾选有时是误操作。
- **列表是记录的归属地。** 智能列表和每日视图汇集条目但不拥有它们；通过视图编辑或完成的条目在其所属列表中变更。在具有夜间重置每日列表的产品中，未完成条目被明确返回其所属列表，而非丢失。
- **紧急程度是派生的，而非分阶段的。** 逾期和今日到期状态由条目的日期属性计算得出；条目上没有用户定义的工作流阶段。多阶段条目生命周期属于任务管理和问题追踪的范畴。
- **重复使条目重新具象化。** 重复条目的下一次出现在完成时出现；已完成的出现保留为历史。重复是条目的属性，而非单独管理的例行程序群体。
- **共享是列表范围且个人化的。** 受邀者操作整个列表；分配将单个条目交给一个人。没有组织架构图角色模型，没有审批步骤，没有超出所有者/受邀者的权限层级。
- **提醒是安全网，而非组织者。** 通知层（时间、位置、重复警报、逾期通知）的存在是为了让“捕获与记忆”真正起作用；它本身不重新排序或重新规划列表。

definition.name: Meeting Action-item Management
definition.overview:
A **Meeting Action-item Management** application is the follow-through system for meetings. Its object of record is the **action item**: a discrete commitment captured from a meeting — what must be done, by whom, by when — held as a persistent record and tracked from open to done.

The problem it solves is specific: meetings produce commitments, and commitments made in meetings evaporate. They live in someone's notebook, in a wall of prose minutes, or in nobody's memory. One vendor in this space frames the pain directly: *"What were those action items from the meeting? Who remembers what they were? Anyone know how to find them?"* Another puts the bar plainly: if a meeting ends without a concise task list, *"it could have been done with an email."*

The defining core is small:

```text
Meeting
└── Action item (persistent tracked record)
    ├── What must be done
    ├── One accountable owner
    ├── Due date
    └── Status, tracked through to closure
        └── traceable back to the meeting where it was raised
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — automated reminders, personal dashboards, cross-meeting projects, minutes publishing, AI extraction from transcripts, sync with task tools — is standard capability in mature products, not what makes the product this Type. The discipline this software encodes is older than software: minutes with an action list (who / what / when), reviewed at the next meeting until everything is closed.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**会议待办事项管理**应用是会议的后续执行系统。其记录对象是**待办事项**：从会议中捕捉到的独立承诺——必须做什么、由谁负责、何时完成——作为持久化记录保存，并追踪其从开启到完成的状态。

它解决的问题非常具体：会议产生承诺，而会议中做出的承诺往往消散无踪。它们存在于某人的笔记本里、存在于大段文字记录的会议纪要中，或者存在于无人记得的记忆里。该领域的一家供应商直接描述了这种痛点：*“会议上的那些待办事项是什么？谁记得它们是什么？有人知道怎么找到它们吗？”* 另一家则直截了当地设定了标准：如果会议结束时没有一份简洁的任务清单，*“那本可以用一封电子邮件解决。”*

其定义性核心很小：

```text
会议
└── 待办事项（持久化追踪记录）
     ├── 必须完成的事项
     ├── 唯一的责任人
     ├── 截止日期
     └── 状态，追踪直至关闭
         └── 可追溯至提出该事项的会议
```

通常与这些产品相关联的其他功能——自动提醒、个人仪表盘、跨会议项目、会议纪要发布、从转录稿中提取AI内容、与任务工具同步——在成熟产品中都是标准能力，而非使该产品成为此类型的特征。该软件所编码的纪律比软件本身更古老：带有行动清单（谁/做什么/何时）的会议纪要，在下次会议上进行回顾，直到所有事项关闭。
definition.dc: The action item is the system's unit of record. Across the researched products it consistently carries:
definition.dc_zh: 行动事项是系统的基本记录单元。在所研究的产品中，它始终包含：
definition.rules:
- **One owner per item.** The strongest written convention in the Type: several people may contribute, but exactly one person is accountable and chaseable. Unowned items undermine the follow-up loop the software exists to run.
- **Status is the operational content.** The system's value is the visible movement of items from assigned to completed; an action list without status tracking is just minutes.
- **Outstanding items resurface by default.** Carry-forward onto the next agenda is automatic in mature products — the review happens because the system forces it, not because anyone remembers.
- **Items link back to their context.** The trail from commitment → discussion → decision stays intact, which is what distinguishes a managed commitment from a floating to-do.
- **Overdue is visible.** Due dates make lateness computable; products flag overdue items and remind owners of upcoming or past-due work.
- **Complementarity with task tools.** Products in this space explicitly position themselves as *not* another task management system: items are captured and governed at the meeting layer, then exported or synced to the execution tools the team already uses.
- **Completion carries evidence.** Owners commonly attach the finished work (document, report, photo) to the item, making the closed item the record of delivery.
definition.rules_zh:
- **每项事项一名责任人。** 该类型中最强的书面惯例：多人可以贡献，但恰好一人负责且可被追责。无主事项会破坏该软件旨在运行的后续循环。
- **状态是操作性内容。** 系统的价值在于事项从分配到完成的可见移动；没有状态追踪的行动清单只是会议纪要。
- **未决事项默认重新浮现。** 在成熟产品中，结转至下次议程是自动的——回顾发生是因为系统强制它发生，而不是因为有人记得。
- **事项链接回其上下文。** 从承诺 → 讨论 → 决策的轨迹保持完整，这是将受管理的承诺与漂浮的待办区分开来的关键。
- **逾期是可见的。** 截止日期使迟到可计算；产品标记逾期事项并提醒责任人即将到期或已过期的工作。
- **与任务工具的互补性。** 该领域的产品明确将自己定位为*不是*另一个任务管理系统：事项在会议层捕捉和治理，然后导出或同步到团队已使用的执行工具。
- **完成携带证据。** 责任人通常将完成的工作（文档、报告、照片）附加到事项上，使关闭的事项成为交付的记录。

definition.name: Meeting Notes Application
definition.overview:
A **Meeting Notes Application** is an application for creating, structuring, and retaining the written record of meetings. It anchors a persistent, human-authored note to a specific identified meeting occurrence, structures the capture around the meeting's own anatomy — the topics planned for the meeting and the decisions and action items that come out of it — and works that record across the meeting's lifecycle: prepare the agenda, capture notes while the meeting happens, finalize and distribute the record to participants, and keep it searchable afterward.

It solves a specific failure pattern: meetings end, and what was discussed, decided, and assigned lives nowhere dependable — scattered across individual memories, private scratchpads, and email threads. This Type of application makes the meeting's record a first-class object: one document per meeting, bound to that meeting, structured so that outcomes (decisions, action items) can be found and followed up later.

The defining core is small:

```text
Meeting occurrence (identified meeting: time, participants, purpose)
└── Meeting note — the persistent, human-authored record of the meeting
    ├── Planned topics (agenda)
    └── Outcomes (decisions, action items) as addressable elements
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — agenda builders, templates, recurring meeting series, email distribution, approval workflows, archives, AI transcription — is standard capability that mature products add, not what makes the product a meeting notes application. A paper minutes book satisfies the same core.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**会议记录应用**是用于创建、组织和保留会议书面记录的应用程序。它将一份持久、由人工撰写的笔记锚定到特定的已识别会议实例上，围绕会议自身的结构来组织记录——即会议计划的主题以及由此产生的决策和行动项——并在会议的生命周期中运作该记录：准备议程，在会议进行时捕捉笔记，最终确定记录并将其分发给参与者，并在之后保持其可搜索性。

它解决了一个特定的失效模式：会议结束后，讨论、决定和分配的内容无处可靠存放——散落在个人记忆、私人草稿本和电子邮件线程中。这种类型的应用程序将会议记录提升为一等对象：每次会议对应一份文档，与该会议绑定，并结构化以便后续能够找到并跟进结果（决策、行动项）。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
会议实例（已识别的会议：时间、参与者、目的）
└── 会议笔记——会议的持久、人工撰写的记录
     ├── 计划主题（议程）
     └── 结果（决策、行动项）作为可寻址元素
```

通常与该类别关联的其他所有内容——议程构建器、模板、定期会议系列、电子邮件分发、审批工作流、归档、AI转录——都是成熟产品添加的标准功能，而非使产品成为会议记录应用的原因。一本纸质会议记录簿同样满足这一核心需求。
definition.dc:
**Meeting occurrence.** The anchor of the whole model. A specific, identified meeting — a date and time, a set of participants, a purpose. The note is *of* this meeting; it is not a topic page or a project document. In most current products the meeting occurrence comes from the organization's calendar (the note is created from or linked to a calendar event); in others the application maintains its own meeting registry, or organizes meetings inside containers for teams or bodies. Conceptually these are the same: an identified gathering that the record hangs from.

**Meeting note.** The unit of record. A persistent document capturing what happened in the meeting — authored and edited by a person in the application, and retained so it can be retrieved later. In the formal pole this document is the *minutes*; in lighter products it is simply the *notes*. The distinction is one of formality, not of structure: both are the meeting's record.

**Meeting anatomy.** The note is not an unstructured page. It is organized around the meeting's own anatomy:

- *Planned topics* — the agenda: what the meeting intended to cover. Notes are taken against these topics; in structured products, notes and decisions attach directly to agenda items.
- *Outcomes* — what the meeting produced. Decisions are recorded as identifiable entries (findable later: "what did we decide about X?"). Action items are recorded with an owner and usually a due date, and behave as addressable elements rather than buried prose.

Remove any leg and the Type collapses: without the meeting anchor it is a generic note-taking or document tool; without the authored record it is a scheduling tool; without the anatomy it is a word processor holding a page titled "meeting".
definition.dc_zh:
**会议发生。** 整个模型的锚点。一个特定、已识别的会议——包括日期和时间、一组参与者、一个目的。笔记是*关于*这个会议的；它不是主题页或项目文档。在大多数当前产品中，会议发生来自组织的日历（笔记从日历事件创建或链接）；在其他产品中，应用维护自己的会议注册，或在团队或机构容器内组织会议。概念上这些是相同的：一个已识别的聚会，记录悬挂于此。

**会议记录。** 记录单元。一个持久文档，捕捉会议中发生的事情——由人在应用中编写和编辑，并保留以便后续检索。在正式场合，这个文档是*会议纪要*；在轻量级产品中，它只是*笔记*。区别在于正式性，而不是结构：两者都是会议的记录。

**会议结构。** 笔记不是无结构页面。它围绕会议自身的结构组织：

- *计划议题* — 议程：会议打算涵盖的内容。针对这些议题做笔记；在结构化产品中，笔记和决策直接附加到议程项目。
- *结果* — 会议产生的内容。决策被记录为可识别条目（便于后续查找：‘我们对X做了什么决定？’）。行动项被记录为任务或后续事项。
definition.rules:
- **The note is bound to the meeting occurrence.** The record inherits the meeting's identity — its date, participants, and purpose. This binding is what makes the archive answerable ("what did we decide in the March meeting?").
- **Action items become trackable the moment they are recorded.** They carry an owner and typically a due date; they appear on the owner's list and survive the meeting that created them.
- **Unfinished business rolls forward.** In products with meeting series, incomplete action items and parked topics from one occurrence are carried into the next — the record chain, not human memory, carries continuity.
- **Access is scoped to the meeting's audience.** The common pattern is that the meeting's participants can see its record, with broader access (managers, governance roles) as an explicit configuration; some products instead default a new note to private-to-author and share it with participants as a deliberate step. Formal products add approval gates and, in some cases, recipient-specific redaction before distribution.
- **Distribution reaches beyond the user base.** Records are commonly sent to participants who hold no account in the application — the record, not the account, is the deliverable.
- **The human is the author.** Whatever assistance the product offers (formatting, templates, AI drafting), the record is something a person takes, corrects, and owns. This is the Type's structural contrast with transcription-centered products.
definition.rules_zh:
- **笔记绑定到会议实例。** 记录继承会议的身份——其日期、参与者和目的。这种绑定使档案可回答（“我们在三月的会议上决定了什么？”）。
- **行动项在记录的那一刻变得可追踪。** 它们携带负责人和通常的截止日期；它们出现在负责人的列表中，并存活于创建它们的会议之后。
- **未决事务向前滚动。** 在具有会议系列的产品中，来自一个实例的不完整行动项和暂存主题会被带入下一个——记录链，而非人类记忆，承载连续性。
- **访问范围限定于会议的受众。** 常见模式是会议的参与者可以查看其记录，更广泛的访问（经理、治理角色）作为显式配置；一些产品则将新笔记默认设为作者私有，并作为有意步骤与参与者共享。正式产品添加审批关卡，在某些情况下，在分发前进行针对收件人的删节。
- **分发超越用户基础。** 记录通常发送给在应用程序中没有账户的参与者——记录，而非账户，是可交付物。
- **人是作者。** 无论产品提供什么辅助（格式化、模板、AI起草），记录都是由人记录、更正和拥有的内容。这是该类型与以转录为中心的产品之间的结构性对比。
