definition.name: Nonprofit Program Management
definition.overview:
A **Nonprofit Program Management** application is the mission-driven organization's system for managing its **programs** — the planned offerings (services, activities, projects) through which the organization delivers its mission — from planning through delivery to performance reporting.

The defining core is small. The system centers on a persistent **program record** for each offering the organization runs, structures the offering's **planned delivery** inside the system (scheduled services and sessions, or workplanned activities and milestones), and **tracks recorded delivery against that plan**, rolling it up as program-level performance for the people who oversee the organization — program leadership, boards, and funders.

Everything else commonly associated with this category — participant enrollment and rosters, attendance, program budgets, indicator libraries, case plans, portals, AI summaries — is standard or optional machinery that mature products add, not what makes the product a program management system. One strong demonstration: a whole class of these products manages programs for international development organizations without tracking any identified person at all — beneficiaries appear only as aggregate counts inside indicator data.

When the center of gravity shifts to the people and their individual service episodes, the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (Nonprofit Case Management, Beneficiary Management); when it shifts to structured results frameworks and indicator actuals as records of their own, it is drifting toward a Monitoring & Evaluation Platform.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **非营利组织项目管理** 应用是使命驱动型组织管理其**项目**的系统——这些项目是组织交付其使命的计划性服务（服务、活动、项目）——涵盖从规划、交付到绩效报告的全过程。

其定义性核心较小。该系统以每个组织运营的项目对应的持久化**项目记录**为中心，在系统内构建项目的**计划交付**（安排的服务和活动场次，或工作计划中的活动与里程碑），并**跟踪相对于计划的已记录交付情况**，将其汇总为项目层面的绩效，供监督组织的人员——项目领导层、董事会和资助方——审阅。

与此类别通常关联的其他一切——参与者注册与名单、出勤、项目预算、指标库、个案计划、门户、AI摘要——都是成熟产品添加的标准或可选功能，并非构成项目管理系统的核心。一个有力的证明是：整个一类此类产品为国际发展组织管理项目，却根本不跟踪任何可识别的个人——受益人仅以指标数据中的汇总计数出现。

当重心转向个人及其单独的服务周期时，该产品就向另一种应用类型（非营利组织个案管理、受益人管理）漂移；当重心转向结构化成果框架和作为独立记录的指标实际值时，它则向监测与评估平台漂移。
definition.dc:
```text
Program (the managed offering of record)
└── Planned delivery elements (what will happen, when)
    └── Delivery records (what happened, attributed to the plan)
        └── Program performance (planned vs recorded, rolled up and reported)
```

Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as program management:

- **Program as the managed offering of record** — a persistent, identified record for each defined program, carrying at minimum an identity, an intent (goals or aims), and a span (period and status). Everything else in the system attaches to this record. Without it there is no offering to manage — only generic tasks or contacts.
- **Planned delivery under the program** — the offering's delivery is structured inside the system as planned elements over time: service schedules and individual sessions in one implementation style; activity workplans with milestones and deliverables over reporting periods in another. Without planning, the program record is a brochure entry and there is nothing to manage.
- **Delivery records attributed to the plan** — execution is recorded in the system (services delivered, sessions held, attendance, milestone completions and sign-offs) and attached to the program's planned elements, so what happened is traceable to what was planned. Without attribution, records are just an activity log.
- **Program performance rollup** — recorded delivery is compared against the plan and surfaced as program-level progress: dashboards, on-track/off-track signals, planned-vs-actual views, and reports directed at management and oversight parties. Without rollup, tracking stays private note-keeping.
definition.dc_zh:
项目（作为管理主记录的服务方案）
└── 计划交付要素（将在何时发生什么）
    └── 交付记录（实际发生了什么，归属于计划）
        └── 项目绩效（计划与实际的对比，汇总并报告）

四个关键属性。若移除任何一个，该产品将无法被识别为项目管理：

- **项目作为管理主记录** —— 每个定义的项目都有一个持久、明确的记录，至少包含一个标识、一个意图（目标或目的）以及一个周期（时间段和状态）。系统中的所有其他内容都附加到此记录。没有它，就没有可管理的服务方案——只有泛化的任务或联系人。
- **项目下的计划交付** —— 服务方案的交付在系统中被构建为随时间推移的计划要素：一种模式下是服务日程安排与单次活动；另一种模式下是包含里程碑与交付物的活动工作计划，并按报告周期划分。没有计划，项目记录就只是一份宣传手册内容，无可管理。
- **归属于计划的交付记录** —— 执行情况被记录在系统中（提供的服务、举办的活动、出席情况、里程碑完成与签收），并附加到项目的计划要素上，因此实际发生的情况可追溯至原计划。没有归属，记录就仅是活动日志。
- **项目绩效（滚动汇总与报告）** —— 系统将各计划要素的“计划”与“实际”记录进行对比、计算并汇总，形成整体项目绩效视图。没有绩效衡量与报告，计划与交付记录就处于割裂状态，无法支持管理决策。
definition.rules:
### Delivery is attributed, not just noted

Delivery records attach to the program's planned elements (a session, a service, a milestone). This attribution rule is what connects daily work to program reporting; products structure their recording screens around it.

### Participation has a lifecycle

In implementations that track identified people, a person's relationship to a program is a managed state — enrolled, active, exited — with exits recorded rather than deleted, so historical counts remain reportable.

### Progress is judged against the plan

The system continuously compares recorded delivery with planned delivery. Off-track conditions are made visible proactively (overdue milestones, over-budget projects, goals not being met) rather than waiting for someone to ask.

### Reporting is built from recorded data

Funder, board, and compliance reports are generated from the delivery records the system already holds — which is why data-quality machinery (duplicates, missing fields) concentrates before reporting deadlines. In the development-sector implementation, partner-submitted data commonly passes through a submission-and-approval step before it counts.

### Programs have a span

A program has a defined period and a status; it is planned, operates, and eventually ends, with its record retained. The system's reporting aggregates respect that span (for example, performance periods with a starting point and an end goal).

### Access follows the structure

Permissions are organized around the program structure: staff see their programs, leadership sees across programs, and partner organizations see and report on only what they carry out. Sensitivity of participant-level data (common in human-services variants) reinforces role-based access.
definition.rules_zh:
### 交付是归因的，而非仅被记录

交付记录依附于项目的计划要素（一个活动场次、一项服务、一个里程碑）。此归因规则将日常项目工作与项目报告连接起来；产品围绕它构建其记录界面。

### 参与度具有生命周期

在跟踪可识别人员的实施方案中，个人与项目的关系是一种被管理的状态——已注册、活跃、已退出——退出被记录而非删除，因此历史计数仍可报告。

### 进展是相对于计划来判断的

系统持续地将记录的交付与计划的交付进行比较。异常情况（逾期的里程碑、超预算的项目、未达成的目标）会被主动呈现出来，而非等待有人提问。

### 报告基于已记录的数据构建

资助方、董事会和合规性报告由系统已持有的交付记录生成——这就是为什么数据质量问题（重复、缺失字段）会在报告截止日期前集中出现。在发展领域的实施方案中，合作伙伴提交的数据通常需经过提交-审批步骤后才能计入。

### 项目具有时间跨度

项目有明确的周期和状态；它被规划、执行，并最终结束，其记录被保留。系统的报告汇总会尊重该时间跨度（例如，具有起点和终点的绩效周期）。

### 访问权限遵循结构

权限围绕项目结构组织：工作人员查看其负责的项目，领导层查看跨项目情况，合作伙伴组织仅查看并报告其执行的部分。参与者层面数据的敏感性（常见于人类服务变体）强化了基于角色的访问控制。

definition.name: Social Impact Measurement
definition.overview:
A **Social Impact Measurement** application is the system a mission-driven organization or funder uses to run its impact measurement practice. It holds the organization's own definition of the change it seeks — outcomes, goals, or population results, with measures attached — as the measurement basis; gathers quantitative and qualitative evidence against that definition from surveys, forms, imports, and partner submissions; and turns the accumulated evidence into stakeholder-facing impact communication: dashboards, impact reports, stories, and public transparency surfaces.

The defining core is small and jointly held:

```text
Impact framework — the change the organization seeks, made measurable
└── Evidence base — quantitative + qualitative data gathered against the framework
    └── Impact communication — dashboards, reports, and stories for funders,
        boards, partners, communities, and the public
```

Remove the framework and only data collection remains. Remove the evidence and only a strategy document remains. Remove the communication loop and only a private data store remains. A product without all three is not recognizable as impact measurement software.

Everything else commonly associated with the category — theory-of-change builders, standards libraries, AI analysis, public dashboards, two-sided funder–grantee workflows — is widespread in current products but is not what makes one an impact measurement tool. A paper theory of change, a spreadsheet of indicator values, and an annual printed impact report satisfy the same core.

The category is distinct from monitoring and evaluation software: an M&E platform is the machinery-first system of record beneath funded program implementation, built so donors can audit the numbers; an impact measurement tool is the practice layer above an organization's own strategy, built so the organization can demonstrate and improve its impact. The boundary is explained in Related Application Types.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**社会影响力测量**应用是使命驱动型组织或资助者用来执行其影响力测量实践的系统。它以组织自身对其所追求变革的定义——结果、目标或人口成果，并附带衡量指标——作为测量依据；通过调查、表单、导入和合作伙伴提交等方式，从该定义中收集定量和定性证据；并将积累的证据转化为面向利益相关者的影响力沟通内容：仪表板、影响力报告、故事和公共透明化界面。

其定义性的核心很小且共同拥有：

```text
影响力框架——组织所追求的变革，使其可衡量
└── 证据基础——根据框架收集的定量 + 定性数据
    └── 面向利益相关者的影响力沟通——为资助者、
        董事会、合作伙伴、社区和公众提供的仪表板、报告和故事
```

移除框架，则只剩下数据收集。移除证据，则只剩下一份战略文件。移除沟通环节，则只剩下一个私有数据存储。一个缺乏这三者中任何一部分的产品，都无法被识别为影响力测量软件。

该类别中其他常被关联的内容——变革理论构建器、标准库、AI分析、公共仪表板、双边的资助者-受资助者工作流程——在当前产品中很普遍，但它们并非使某个工具成为影响力测量工具的本质。一份纸面的变革理论、一张指标值的电子表格和一份年度印刷的影响力报告同样满足了这个核心。

该类别与监测和评估软件不同：M&E平台是资助项目实施之下的以机制为先的记录系统，其构建是为了让捐助者能够审计数据；而影响力测量工具则是组织自身战略之上的实践层，其构建是为了让组织能够展示和改进其影响力。其边界在“相关应用类型”中进行了解释。
definition.dc:
**1. The impact framework — the measurement basis.**

The organizing structure is the organization's own statement of intended change with measures attached. Products realize it in different vocabularies: a theory of change whose outcomes carry tag taxonomies; a set of metrics or key impact indicators standardized across a portfolio; a scorecard of population results and indicators beside program performance measures; per-person outcome assessments. Two properties matter more than the vocabulary:

- the framework is **self-defined** — the organization's or funder's impact strategy, optionally mapped to shared standards, not a donor's mandated plan of record; and
- the framework is **held as managed records, not a diagram** — the measures are objects the system can collect data against, aggregate, and report on.

**2. The evidence base — gathered against the framework.**

Impact evidence is multi-source by nature, and the category treats quantitative and qualitative material as parallel citizens:

- quantitative measures — counts, percentages, ratings, financial figures — entered directly, collected through surveys and forms, or imported from spreadsheets and other systems;
- qualitative evidence — open-ended survey responses, interviews, testimonials, photos, narrative reports — captured, coded or tagged against the framework's outcomes, and made as analyzable as the numbers.

Evidence is organized so it can answer the framework's questions and trace back to its sources: which person, program, grantee, or document a number or a quote came from.

**3. The impact communication loop.**

The accumulated evidence is turned into outputs aimed at people outside the measurement team: dashboards for staff and leadership, designed impact reports for boards and donors, stories that pair numbers with human testimony, and public transparency surfaces that update as data changes. The purpose is demonstration and mobilization — proving impact to secure funding and trust, and feeding what was learned back into the work. This loop is what separates impact measurement from record-keeping.
definition.dc_zh:
**1. 影响力框架——衡量基础。**

组织结构是组织自身关于预期变革的陈述，并附有衡量指标。产品以不同词汇体系实现：一种理论变革模型，其成果携带标签分类法；一套在项目组合中标准化的度量指标或关键影响力指标；一份人口结果与指标记分卡，与项目绩效度量并列；个人成果评估。有两个属性比词汇本身更重要：

- 该框架是**自定义的**——是组织或资助方的影响力策略，可选择性地与共享标准对应，而非捐赠方强制规定的计划记录；且
- 该框架**以受控记录形式存在，而非图表**——这些度量指标是系统能够收集数据、汇总并生成报告的实体对象。

**2. 证据基础——依据框架收集。**

影响力证据本质上是多源的，该类别将定量和定性材料视为同等重要的组成部分：

- **定量度量**——计数、百分比、评级、财务数据——直接录入、通过问卷和表格收集，或从电子表格及其他系统导入；

- **定性证据**——开放式问卷回复、访谈、证言、照片、叙述性报告——被捕捉、编码或标记到框架的成果下，并使其具有与数字数据同等的可分析性。
definition.rules:
**Measures are defined before data.** The framework is the measurement basis: what can be collected, aggregated, and reported follows from what was defined. Changing a measure with history behind it is a governed act — products preserve the record and let the framework evolve without destroying past evidence.

**Qualitative evidence is a first-class citizen.** Stories, open text, and testimonials are not decoration; they are coded, counted, and charted beside the numbers. This is a structural signature of the category — the human testimony is treated as assessment, not as illustration.

**Comparability and flexibility are held in tension.** Funder-side products standardize a core metric set across a portfolio for aggregate reporting while deliberately leaving room for program-specific measures and storytelling. The framework is expected to serve both the portfolio roll-up and the individual program's story.

**Evidence must be defensible.** Outputs are built for scrutiny by boards, funders, and the public; products emphasize traceability from every reported figure back to its source evidence. Where submissions flow between organizations, approval flows let both sides refine answers together — collaboration-shaped governance rather than audit-lock.

**Reporting burden is a design constraint.** In funder-run deployments, question sets are tailored so each grantee sees only what is relevant to it, submitters keep their own history and reuse prior answers, and products explicitly market the submitter's side as valuable in itself. A measurement network that treats grantees as data pipes tends to fail adoption.

**Beneficiary data is sensitive.** The evidence base contains data about vulnerable people; access control, sharing rules, and security certification are standard furniture, and public surfaces are configured to expose results without exposing underlying records.

**Vocabulary follows methodology.** Organizations measure under different frameworks and names; products accommodate this rather than enforce one vocabulary — some products even let customers rename the system's own objects to match their methodology.
definition.rules_zh:
**衡量指标在数据之前定义。** 框架是测量基础：可以收集、汇总和报告的内容取决于定义的内容。更改带有历史记录的衡量指标是一项受治理的行动——产品会保留记录，并允许框架演进而不破坏过去的证据。

**定性证据是一等公民。** 故事、开放文本和证词不是装饰品；它们被编码、计数，并与数字并列绘制图表。这是该类别一个结构性特征——人类证词被视为评估，而非说明。

**可比性和灵活性之间存在张力。** 资助方的产品为整个投资组合标准化核心指标集以便汇总报告，同时刻意为项目特定的衡量指标和叙事留出空间。该框架需要同时服务于投资组合汇总和单个项目的叙述。

**证据必须是可辩护的。** 输出物是为了接受董事会、资助者和公众的审查而构建的；产品强调从每个报告的数字追溯到其源证据的可追溯性。在组织之间存在提交流的情况下，审批流允许双方共同完善答案——协作型治理而非审计锁定。

**报告负担是一个设计约束。** 在资助者运营的部署中，问题集被定制，使每个受资助者仅看到与其相关的内容，提交者保留自己的历史记录并重用之前的答案，产品明确地将提交者侧宣传为本身就有价值。一个将受资助者视为数据管道的测量网络往往难以成功采用。

**受益人数据是敏感的。** 证据基础包含关于弱势群体的数据；访问控制、共享规则和安全认证是标准配置

definition.name: Sponsorship Management
definition.overview:
A **Sponsorship Management** application is an organization's system of record for running a sponsorship program: it holds the sponsors (external companies that pay for visibility and benefits), defines the sponsorship offerings that can be sold, records each sponsorship commitment with both the money owed to the organization and the benefits owed to the sponsor, tracks the delivery of those benefits, and carries the sponsor relationship from one term to the next.

The defining core is small:

```text
Sponsor (external organization paying for benefits)
└── Sponsorship offering (priced package of defined benefits)
    └── Commitment of record (sponsor × offering)
        ├── money side   → invoiced / collected
        └── benefit side → tracked to delivery
            └── renewal or close
```

Everything else commonly bundled with these products — application and approval workflows, online sponsorship galleries, e-signed contracts, ROI dashboards, ad placements, two-sided sponsor marketplaces — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a sponsorship manager. A product in which staff record sponsors, define benefit packages, and carry each commitment through payment and benefit delivery is fully this Type even without any of the extras.

The Type exists because a sponsorship is a **two-sided exchange**, not a gift. A donor gives money and receives gratitude; a sponsor pays money and is owed specific, deliverable benefits — a logo placement, a booth-side banner, event tickets, a named recognition level. The system's job is to hold both sides of that exchange on one record and make sure neither side is dropped.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**赞助管理**应用是组织管理赞助项目的权威系统：它管理赞助商（为获取可见性和权益付费的外部公司）、定义可供销售的赞助产品、记录每项赞助承诺（包括组织应收款项和应付给赞助商的权益）、跟踪这些权益的交付情况，并将赞助关系延续至下一个周期。

其核心定义要素很简单：

```text
赞助商（付费获取权益的外部组织）
└── 赞助产品（具有定价和明确权益的套餐）
    └── 承诺记录（赞助商 × 产品）
        ├── 款项端 → 已开票/已收款
        └── 权益端 → 跟踪至交付
            └── 续约或关闭
```

其他常与此类产品捆绑的功能——申请与审批流程、在线赞助展示、电子签合同、ROI仪表板、广告位投放、双边赞助市场——在当前产品中普遍存在，但并非定义“赞助管理器”产品的本质。一个产品只要能让员工记录赞助商、定义权益套餐、并让每项承诺完成付款和权益交付流程，即使没有任何额外功能，也完全属于此**类型**。

此类型存在的原因在于，赞助是一种**双向交换**，而非捐赠。捐赠者付出金钱并获得感谢；赞助商支付款项，并应获得具体、可交付的权益——例如标志展示、展位旁横幅、活动门票、冠名认可等级。系统的职责是将交换双方记录在同一条目中，并确保任何一方都不会被遗漏。
definition.dc:
Three structures, held jointly:

**The sponsor.** An identified external organization — a company, a local business, a corporate partner — held as a persistent record. The sponsor is the counterparty of the exchange: it provides money (or resources) and is owed benefits. In membership-based organizations the sponsor is frequently also a member or contact in the same database, and its sponsorship history accumulates on its record.

**The sponsorship offering.** A defined, priced package — often called a sponsorship opportunity, level, or package — whose content is a set of benefits: recognition (naming rights, logo placement, sponsor levels), visibility (website showcase, program ads, banners), access (tickets, invitations), and deliverable items. Offerings are what the organization sells; they can be organized into levels (title/platinum/silver-style tiers), bundled with add-ons, priced differently for members and non-members, and limited in quantity.

**The commitment of record.** When a sponsor takes an offering, a persistent record is created binding that sponsor to that offering for a term or occasion. The commitment carries both sides of the exchange:

- the **money side** — the amount, the invoice, the payment status;
- the **benefit side** — the specific benefits owed and their delivery state.

The commitment advances through a lifecycle — committed → paid → fulfilled → recognized — and closes either at renewal (the sponsor takes an offering again next term) or at close. Completed commitments remain as history: they feed renewal conversations, revenue reporting, and the sponsor's record.
definition.dc_zh:
三大共同结构：

**赞助商。** 一个已识别的外部组织——可以是一家公司、本地企业或合作伙伴——作为持久记录保留。赞助商是交换的对立方：它提供资金（或资源），并享有应得的利益。在会员制组织中，赞助商通常同时也是同一数据库中的会员或联系人，其赞助历史会累积在记录上。

**赞助包。** 一个已定义、定价的套餐——通常称为赞助机会、级别或套餐——其内容是一系列权益：认可（冠名权、Logo展示、赞助商级别）、曝光（网站展示、节目广告、横幅）、访问权（门票、邀请函）以及可交付物品。赞助包是组织销售的产品；可按级别组织（如冠名/铂金/白银等级别）、与附加服务捆绑、为会员和非会员设置不同价格，并可限量供应。

**承诺记录。** 当赞助商接受某个赞助包时，会创建一条持久记录，将该赞助商与该赞助包在特定期限或活动中绑定。此承诺承载交换的双方：
- **资金方** —— 金额、发票、支付状态；
- **权益方** —— 应得的具体权益及其交付状态。
承诺会经历一个生命周期：已承诺 → 已支付 → 已履行 →
definition.rules:
### Benefits are obligations

The structural rule of the Type: every benefit in a sold package is owed. Fulfillment tracking exists because undelivered benefits are broken promises with renewal consequences. This is the behavioral line between sponsorship and donation handling.

### Sponsorship money is revenue, not a gift

Sponsorship payments are recorded and reported as revenue from an exchange. In nonprofit settings this distinguishes sponsorship from charitable contributions, which follow different recognition and receipting treatment. In the researched sample, fundraising and sponsorship live in separate machinery — a separation that follows from the exchange-vs-gift distinction rather than from convention.

### Offerings can be scarce

Packages and items commonly carry quantity limits — a single title sponsorship, a bounded number of banner placements — so availability is part of the offering's state, and a sold-out item stops being sellable.

### Pricing follows membership

In membership-based organizations, the same offering commonly carries a member price and a non-member price; sponsorship itself is a classic non-dues revenue line, and member sponsors may receive pricing as a membership benefit.

### Approval can gate the commitment

Where sponsors apply rather than buy outright, the commitment is not created until staff approve; application states (submitted, approved, declined) are part of the workflow.

### The record compounds

Completed commitments are retained: they are the basis for renewal offers, the sponsor's history, and the revenue picture presented to boards. A sponsorship program's value in the system grows with its history.

### Event binding is optional, not required

Sponsorships may attach to a specific event or program, or stand as organization-level annual commitments. The same system commonly holds both.
definition.rules_zh:
### 权益是义务

该类型的结构性规则：已售套餐中的每项权益都是应履行的义务。需要进行交付跟踪，因为未交付的权益是失信行为，会影响续约。这是赞助与捐赠处理方式在行为上的分界线。

### 赞助款项是收入，而非礼物

赞助付款作为交换收入进行记录和报告。在非营利环境中，这区分了赞助与慈善捐赠，后者遵循不同的认可和收据处理方式。在研究样本中，筹款和赞助由独立机制处理——这种区分源于交换与礼物的本质差异，而非惯例。

### 产品可能具有稀缺性

套餐和物品通常带有数量限制——如唯一的冠名赞助、有限数量的横幅广告位——因此可用性是产品状态的一部分，售罄的物品将停止销售。

### 定价依据会员资格

在基于会员的组织中，同一产品通常有会员价和非会员价；赞助本身是经典的非会费收入来源，会员赞助商可能获得作为会员福利的定价优惠。

### 审批可作为承诺的关卡

当赞助商是申请而非直接购买时，承诺在员工批准前不会创建；申请状态（已提交、已批准、已拒绝）是工作流的一部分。

### 记录具有累积性

已完成的承诺会被保留：它们是续约报价、赞助商历史以及提交给董事会的收入概览的基础。赞助项目在系统中的价值随其历史积累而增长。

### 活动绑定是可选项，非必需

赞助可关联特定活动或项目，也可作为组织

definition.name: Standards Development Platform
definition.overview:
A **Standards Development Platform** is a collaborative platform used by Standards Development Organizations (SDOs) to manage the full lifecycle of creating, reviewing, approving, and publishing technical standards.

The defining structure is:

```text
Standard/Project of record
└── Committee/Working Group (identified participants)
    └── Draft document (with version history)
        └── Comment/Feedback (with disposition tracking)
            └── Consensus mechanism (ballot/vote)
```

The platform supports the structured process by which technical experts develop consensus-based specifications — standards, codes, protocols, or guidelines — that guide design practices, manufacturing methods, construction quality, operational safety, or interoperability across industries.

When the dominant surface shifts to governance of people without technical content lifecycle, the product is drifting toward Committee Management. When it shifts to generic document storage without consensus machinery, it becomes Document Management. When it certifies people or products against existing standards rather than creating them, it becomes Certification Management.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **标准开发平台** 是标准开发组织（SDOs）用来管理创建、审查、批准和发布技术标准整个生命周期的协作平台。

其定义性结构是：

```text
标准/在制项目
└── 委员会/工作组（已确认的参与者）
    └── 草案文件（含版本历史）
        └── 意见/反馈（含处理跟踪）
            └── 共识机制（投票/表决）
```

该平台支持技术专家通过结构化流程开发基于共识的规范——标准、规范、协议或指南——这些规范指导设计实践、制造方法、建筑质量、操作安全或跨行业的互操作性。

当主导界面转向对人员的治理而非技术内容生命周期时，产品会偏向委员会管理。当转向通用文档存储而缺乏共识机制时，它就变成了文档管理。当依据现有标准认证人员或产品，而不是创建标准时，它就成为了认证管理。
definition.dc:
```text
Standard/Project of record
└── Committee/Working Group (identified participants)
    └── Draft document (with version history)
        └── Comment/Feedback (with disposition tracking)
            └── Consensus mechanism (ballot/vote)
```

Five properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a Standards Development Platform:

- **Standard/Project of record** — A persistent identified record of a standards development effort, carrying scope, owner, and a lifecycle from proposal to publication. Without this, the product becomes generic document collaboration.
- **Committee/Working Group** — A group of identified participants (experts, members, organizations) authorized to develop the standard. Without this, the product becomes individual authoring.
- **Draft document with version history** — The evolving technical content, with tracked changes and versions. Without this, the product becomes meeting minutes or a task tracker.
- **Comment/Feedback mechanism** — A structured way for participants to provide feedback on the draft, with disposition tracking (accepted, revised, rejected). Without this, the product becomes document approval without feedback.
- **Consensus mechanism (ballot/vote)** — A formal or informal process to determine whether the draft has achieved consensus and can advance. Without this, the product becomes a document repository without consensus.
definition.dc_zh:
正式记录的标准/项目
└── 委员会/工作组（特定参与者）
    └── 草案文件（含版本历史）
        └── 意见/反馈（含处理情况追踪）
            └── 共识机制（表决/投票）
definition.rules:
### Lifecycle stages are gated

A project cannot advance to the next stage without meeting defined criteria (e.g., working group consensus, ballot approval, procedural review). The platform enforces these gates and prevents premature advancement.

### Ballot groups must be balanced

In many SDOs, no single interest category (e.g., producer, user, general interest) can comprise more than one-third of the ballot group. The platform tracks interest categories and alerts when balance is at risk.

### Comments must be dispositioned

Every comment submitted during a ballot or review period must be reviewed and dispositioned (accepted, revised, or rejected) with a rationale. Unresolved comments block advancement.

### Substantive changes require recirculation

If substantive changes are made to the draft after a ballot, a recirculation ballot is required to give voters an opportunity to review and respond to the changes.

### Roles and permissions change by stage

A participant's capabilities depend on their role and the project's current stage. For example, a working group member may be able to edit the draft during the preparatory stage but only comment during the enquiry stage.

### Procedural compliance is verified

Before publication, a review committee (e.g., IEEE RevCom, ISO CS) verifies that all procedural requirements have been met (proper balloting, comment resolution, balance, etc.).
definition.rules_zh:
### 生命周期阶段有门控

项目必须满足定义的标准（如工作组共识、投票批准、程序审查）才能进入下一阶段。平台执行这些门控并防止过早推进。

### 投票小组必须平衡

在许多SDO中，单一利益类别（如生产者、用户、公共利益）不得超过投票小组的三分之一。平台跟踪利益类别并在平衡面临风险时发出警报。

### 意见必须被处理

在投票或审查期间提交的每条意见都必须被审查并处理（接受、修改或拒绝），并需给出理由。未处理的意见将阻止推进。

### 实质性修改需重新传阅

如果在投票后对草案进行实质性修改，则需要进行重新传阅投票，以让投票者有机会审查并回应这些修改。

### 角色和权限随阶段变化

参与者的能力取决于其角色和项目的当前阶段。例如，工作组成员可能在准备阶段可以编辑草案，但在征询阶段只能提交意见。

### 程序合规性需验证

发布前，审查委员会（如IEEE RevCom、ISO CS）会验证所有程序要求是否已满足（正确的投票、意见处理、平衡等）。

definition.name: Member Benefits Management
definition.overview:
A **Member Benefits Management** application is the system a membership organization uses to define, operate, and account for **what membership entitles people to** — negotiated discounts, services, access entitlements, and member-only programs — together with the program machinery through which members verify their standing and redeem those benefits.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Membership standing (who belongs, at what type or level)
└── Benefit offerings of record
    (each with a provider or subject, terms & conditions, and an eligibility scope)
    └── Verify & redeem
        (member proves standing through the program; benefit exercised via a program-controlled mechanism)
        └── Program record (the exercised act leaves its trace)
```

Everything commonly associated with modern benefits programs — white-label member marketplaces, mobile apps, location-aware deal feeds, provider portals, savings dashboards — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. A paper-era membership organization operating a membership card, a set of negotiated rate agreements, and a printed benefit directory fits the same structure without any of them.

When the center of gravity shifts to value *earned* through purchases, the product is drifting toward a different Application Type (Loyalty Program Management). When it shifts to administering insurance or retirement *plans* for employees, that is the employer-benefits territory of a different Type.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**会员权益管理**应用，是会员制组织用来定义、运营和核算**会员资格所赋予的权利**——谈判折扣、服务、访问权限以及会员专属计划——以及会员验证资格和兑换权益所使用的一套计划机制的系统。

其定义性结构如下：

```text
会员资格状态（谁属于会员，属于何种类型或等级）
└── 在册权益提供
    （每项提供都有供应商或主题、条款与条件，以及适用范围）
    └── 验证与兑换
        （会员通过计划证明其资格；权益通过计划控制的机制行使）
        └── 计划记录（行使行为留下痕迹）
```

与现代权益计划常见的关联要素——白标会员市场、移动应用、基于位置的优惠推送、供应商门户、省钱仪表盘——在当今产品中普遍存在，但并非其定义性核心的一部分。一个仅运营会员卡、一套谈判费率协议和一本印刷权益目录的纸质时代会员制组织，即使不包含以上任何要素，也符合同一结构。

当重心转向通过消费**赚取**的价值时，该产品便开始向不同的应用类型（忠诚度计划管理）偏移。当重心转向为员工管理保险或退休**计划**时，则进入了不同类型的雇主福利领域。
definition.dc:
Three jointly-held structures. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as member benefits management:

- **Benefit offerings of record** — each benefit (a discount, a service, an access entitlement, an insurance-style program, member-only content) is held as a persistent, individually identified record carrying a provider or subject, terms and conditions — including validity windows where applicable — and an eligibility scope. Without this, there is nothing to administer: the product degenerates into a deals page, a coupon site, or a bare membership roster.
- **Membership-derived eligibility** — a benefit is exercisable *by virtue of belonging*. What gates use is the organization's membership status and type, not points, purchases, or public availability. Without this, the product becomes retail loyalty or a public coupon marketplace.
- **The verify-and-redeem loop** — the member proves their standing through the program (member login, organizational sign-on, member card or ID) and exercises the benefit through a mechanism the program issues or controls: an authenticated access grant, a code, a link, a ticket, a coupon, or presentation of the member card. Without this, the product is a printed benefits brochure or a static perk list — announced value with no operating machinery.
definition.dc_zh:
三个共同持有的结构。如果移除任何一个，产品将不再被视为会员权益管理：
- **福利记录条目** — 每个福利（如折扣、服务、访问权、保险式计划、会员专属内容）都作为一个持久、独立标识的记录保存，包含提供商或主题、条款和条件——包括适用时的有效期窗口——以及资格范围。没有这一点，就没有可管理的内容：产品退化为交易页面、优惠券网站或单纯的会员名册。
- **基于会员资格的资格** — 福利的行使*基于归属*。控制使用的是组织的会员状态和类型，而不是积分、购买或公开可用性。没有这一点，产品就变成了零售忠诚计划或公共优惠券市场。
- **验证与兑换循环** — 会员通过计划证明其身份（会员登录、组织登录、会员卡或ID），并通过计划发放或控制的机制行使福利：经过验证的访问授权、代码、链接、门票、优惠券或出示会员卡。没有这一点，产品就是印刷的福利手册或静态福利列表——宣布了价值但没有运行机制。
definition.rules:
### Eligibility follows membership standing

Access to the program and to individual benefits is keyed to the organization's membership status. Mature products commonly re-evaluate access on status transitions — a lapsed or pending member is typically excluded from member-only benefits until standing is restored. Exact status vocabularies vary by product.

### Benefits are exercised, not earned

The entitlement exists by belonging. Nothing in the core model accumulates through purchases or activity; programs that introduce earn-and-burn economics have crossed into loyalty-program territory (some products offer such modules alongside).

### Terms and validity govern redemption

An offering's conditions — discount scope, restrictions, expiry — are part of the record and surface at redemption. Offers expire; expired offers are withdrawn from the member-facing catalog.

### Gated offers are protected

Privately negotiated offers are commonly kept inside the gated, authenticated program rather than exposed publicly; organizations decide what is visible, and dedicated products provide per-program content restriction as a first-class control.

### The program does not own the member

Member identity and standing remain anchored in the organization's membership systems; the program references them. Benefits can be run from a standalone platform precisely because eligibility is delegated to the organization of record.

### Redemption is program-mediated

Benefits are redeemed through mechanisms the program issues or controls, not anonymously outside it. This is what distinguishes an operating program from a published list of perks — and it is what makes participation and redemption reporting possible where products offer it.
definition.rules_zh:
### 适用性遵循会员资格状态

对计划及各项权益的访问权限，取决于组织的会员身份状态。成熟产品通常会在状态转换时重新评估访问权限——失效或待处理的会员通常被排除在会员专属权益之外，直到资格状态恢复。具体的状态词汇因产品而异。

### 权益是行使的，而非赚取的

权利因归属而存在。核心模型中没有任何东西是通过购买或活动积累的；引入“赚取与消耗”经济机制的计划已跨入忠诚度计划领域（有些产品会在旁边提供此类模块）。

### 条款与有效期管理兑换

提供的条件——折扣范围、限制、有效期——是记录的一部分，并在兑换时显示。优惠会过期；过期的优惠会从面向会员的目录中撤下。

### 受控优惠受到保护

私下谈判的优惠通常保留在受控的、需要身份验证的计划内部，而非公开暴露；组织决定哪些内容可见，专用产品提供按计划的内容限制作为首要控制功能。

### 计划不拥有会员

会员身份和状态仍锚定在组织的会员系统中；计划只是引用它们。权益可以从独立平台运行，正是因为适用性被委托给了记录组织。

### 兑换通过计划机制

权益是通过计划发放或控制的机制进行兑换的，而非在其外部匿名进行。这正是运作中的计划与发布的福利清单的区别所在——也是当产品提供相关功能时，参与和兑换报告得以实现的基础。

definition.name: Pastoral Care Management
definition.overview:
A **Pastoral Care Management** application is the church-side system for organizing how a congregation cares for its people: it records who needs care, assigns that care to specific caregivers, records the care actually given — visits, calls, cards, conversations, prayers — and keeps the care moving through follow-up until the need resolves. Its records are treated as sensitive pastoral information, held under visibility restricted to those entrusted with the care.

The defining core is small. Three structures must be present together:

```text
Care need, anchored to an identified person
└── Assigned caregiving loop (named caregiver → contact → follow-up → resolution)
    └── Person-bound, visibility-restricted care record
```

- **Care need anchored to an identified person** — an illness, hospitalization, bereavement, absence, crisis, counseling need, or prayer request, recorded against a specific person from the congregation's people records. Guests and non-members can be care subjects too.
- **Assigned caregiving loop** — responsibility for the need is given to a named caregiver (a pastor, a staff member, or a lay caregiver). The work appears on that person's list, contact is made, and follow-up continues until the need is resolved. Responsibility can be transferred or delegated.
- **Person-bound, visibility-restricted care record** — every care contact becomes a durable note attached to the person's record, visible only to people with the appropriate care role, accumulating over time as the person's care history.

Remove the person anchor and it becomes generic task management. Remove the assignment and loop and it becomes a prayer list. Remove the record and the loop becomes ephemeral to-do tracking. Remove the visibility restriction and the pastoral-confidentiality dimension collapses into ordinary contact notes.

The dominant packaging today is inside a Church Management System — either as a named care module or as care workflows configured over the church's people records. The packaging varies by product; the care loop itself does not.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**Pastoral Care Management**应用是教会方面的系统，用于组织会众如何照顾其成员：它记录谁需要照顾，将照顾分配给特定的照顾者，记录实际提供的照顾——探访、电话、卡片、对话、祈祷——并通过跟进保持照顾进行，直到需求得到解决。其记录被视为敏感的牧养信息，仅对被委托照顾的人可见。

其定义核心很小。三个结构必须同时存在：

```text
照顾需求，锚定到已识别的人
└── 分配的照顾循环（指定的照顾者 → 联系 → 跟进 → 解决）
    └── 人员绑定、可见性受限的照顾记录
```

- **锚定到已识别的人的照顾需求** — 疾病、住院、丧亲、缺席、危机、咨询需求或祈祷请求，记录在会众人员记录中的特定个人。访客和非成员也可以是照顾对象。
- **分配的照顾循环** — 需求的责任被赋予指定的照顾者（牧师、工作人员或平信徒照顾者）。工作出现在该人的列表上，进行联系，并跟进直到需求解决。责任可以转移或委托。
- **人员绑定、可见性受限的照顾记录** — 每个照顾联系都成为附在该人记录上的持久笔记，仅对具有适当照顾角色的人可见，随着时间的推移积累为该人的照顾历史。

移除人员锚定，它就变成通用任务管理。移除分配和循环，它就变成祈祷列表。移除记录，循环就变成临时待办事项跟踪。移除可见性限制，牧养机密性维度就崩溃成普通联系笔记。

当前主流包装是在教会管理系统内——要么作为命名的照顾模块，要么作为在教会人员记录上配置的照顾工作流。包装因产品而异；照顾循环本身则不然。
definition.dc: The unit of work is a care need bound to one person: "check on this family," "visit this hospitalized member," "follow up with this guest." One need involves one care subject; when many people need the same contact (for example, Sunday's guests), the system holds one care item per person rather than one shared item. A need reaches the system by referral (staff or leader enters it), by detection (an attendance lapse or a form), or by self-submission (most commonly a prayer request). Categories — hospitalization, bereavement, new guest, prayer request, and similar — are commonly attached to make care searchable and reportable.
definition.dc_zh: 工作单元是一个与个人绑定的关怀需求：'探访这个家庭'，'访问这位住院成员'，'跟进这位访客'。一个需求涉及一个关怀对象；当许多人需要相同的联系（例如，周日的访客），系统为每个人保存一个关怀项目，而不是一个共享项目。一个需求通过推荐（工作人员或负责人输入）、检测（出勤缺失或表单）或自我提交（最常见的是祷告请求）到达系统。类别——住院、丧亲、新访客、祷告请求和类似——通常被附加，以使关怀可搜索和可报告。
definition.rules:
- **Confidentiality is structural, not incidental.** Care records can be restricted to specific care roles; guidance in the most deeply documented implementations warns explicitly against recording confidential content outside that restriction. In at least those implementations, once a record is restricted, users without the role cannot even see that a contact occurred. Staff-level access does not automatically equal access to restricted pastoral records.
- **The record is the deliverable.** In documented implementations, a care assignment is completed by recording the contact that was made — the note lands on the care subject's record, and the assignment cannot be closed without it. This keeps the care history complete by construction.
- **Open care stays visible.** Incomplete care items persist on both the caregiver's work list and the care subject's record until completed; they are findable by coordinators. Care that is assigned but never recorded is detectable.
- **One need, one person.** Care items are about a single person; bulk needs (guest follow-up after a service) are realized as per-person items so each person's care history is complete.
- **Care attaches to people, wherever they are in the church's records.** Guests and non-members can be care subjects; membership is not a prerequisite for care.
- **Responsibility is delegable.** Ownership of a care item can transfer without losing the record; delegation chains (coordinator → group leader → lay caregiver) are a common pattern in larger churches.
definition.rules_zh:
- **机密性是结构性的，而非偶然的。** 照顾记录可以限制为特定的照顾角色；在最深入文档化的实现中，指导明确警告不要在该限制之外记录机密内容。至少在那些实现中，一旦记录被限制，没有该角色的用户甚至无法看到联系已经发生。员工级别的访问权限并不自动等同于对受限牧养记录的访问权限。
- **记录是可交付成果。** 在文档化的实现中，照顾分配通过记录所做的联系来完成——笔记落在照顾对象的记录上，没有它分配就无法关闭。这通过构造保持照顾历史的完整性。
- **开放照顾保持可见。** 未完成的照顾项在照顾者的工作列表和照顾对象的记录上都持续存在，直到完成；它们可以被协调员找到。被分配但从未记录的照顾是可以检测到的。
- **一个需求，一个人。** 照顾项关于单个人；批量需求（服务后的访客跟进）作为每人一项实现，这样每个人的照顾历史都是完整的。
- **照顾附着在人身上，无论他们在教会记录中的位置。** 访客和非成员可以是照顾对象；成员资格不是照顾的前提条件。
- **责任可以委托。** 照顾项的所有权可以在不丢失记录的情况下转移；委托链（协调员 → 小组长 → 平信徒照顾者）在大型教会中是常见模式。

definition.name: Worship Presentation Software
definition.overview:
A **Worship Presentation Software** is the live in-service display system of a worshiping congregation: the application an operator runs *during* a worship service to put song lyrics, scripture, videos, images, and sermon support onto the screens the congregation watches, in real time, following the flow of the service.

Its defining core is small:

```text
Worship content library
└── Service presentation (ordered cue list for a dated service occasion)
    └── Live cueing loop
        └── Operator surface separated from the audience output
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — stage monitors, livestream lyric outputs, countdown clocks, remote apps, licensed song catalogs, cloud sync — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product this Type. A product without any of those extras, operated from a single computer with one projector, is still fully this Type; a product with all of them but no accumulating worship library and no live operator cueing is not.
definition.overview_zh:
一种**敬拜演示软件**是敬拜集会的现场礼拜显示系统：操作员在礼拜进行时使用的应用程序，将歌词、经文、视频、图像和讲道辅助内容实时投放到会众观看的屏幕上，遵循礼拜流程。

其定义的核心很小：

```text
敬拜内容库
└── 礼拜演示（为特定日期的礼拜场合排序的提示列表）
    └── 现场提示循环
        └── 操作员界面与观众输出分离
```

与此类别通常相关的所有其他功能——舞台显示器、直播歌词输出、倒计时钟、远程应用程序、授权歌曲目录、云同步——在当前产品中普遍存在，但这并非使该产品成为此类型的关键。没有任何这些额外功能、仅从一台计算机和一个投影仪操作的产品，仍然是完全符合此类型的产品；反之，拥有所有这些功能但没有积累的敬拜库和现场操作员提示功能的产品则不属于此类型。
definition.dc:
**1. The worship content library.** The product holds reusable, display-ready worship content as a searchable library. Three content kinds recur across every researched product:

- **Songs with lyric text** — the central library item. A song is stored as structured lyric blocks (verse, chorus, bridge) rather than as one flat text, so the operator can display the congregation through it block by block. Songs carry author and copyright information, because projected lyrics carry display obligations.
- **Scripture passages** — retrieved **by reference** (book, chapter, verse) from built-in or imported Bible translations, and rendered into display-ready text automatically. Reference-addressed retrieval is what makes scripture a library item rather than pasted text.
- **Media** — images and videos: motion or still backgrounds placed behind text, clips played at moments in the service.

Many products add further library kinds — announcements, liturgical texts, imported slide decks, pictures — but songs, scripture, and media are the constant trio.

**2. The service presentation.** The central working object is an **ordered cue list for one dated service occasion**, assembled by dragging items out of the library and arranging them in the order the service will follow. The vocabulary varies by product — schedule, presentation, cues, service — but the structure is the same: a sequence of display items for one gathering, built before the service and run during it. This is not a slide deck in the office-presentation sense: the items are pointers into the library (this song, this passage, this video), not self-contained authored pages, and the same song or passage reappears in many services over time.

**3. The live cueing loop with separated surfaces.** During the service, the operator advances through the cue list in real time. Two surfaces are structurally separated:

- the **operator's control view** — showing the cue list, a preview of what each item will look like, what is live now, and what comes next;
- the **audience output** — showing only what is live, clean of operator machinery.

The operator can also step *inside* an item (advancing a song's lyric blocks one at a time), jump ahead or back, insert something on the fly when the service departs from plan, and clear the screen instantly. This operator/audience separation is the category's founding idea and its clearest structural difference from office presentation software.

**Domain binding.** The content and the occasion are worship-service content and occasions. That binding is what makes the library a *worship* library (lyrics with copyright, scripture by reference) and the cue list a *service*.
definition.dc_zh:
**1. 礼拜内容库。** 产品持有可重用的、显示就绪的礼拜内容作为可搜索库。三种内容类型在每个研究的产品中重现：

- **带歌词的歌曲** — 核心库项目。歌曲存储为结构化的歌词块（如主歌、副歌、桥段），而非单一平面文本，使操作员能够逐块向会众显示。歌曲包含作者和版权信息，因为投影歌词具有显示义务。

- **经文段落** — 通过引用（书、章、节）从内置或导入的圣经译本中检索，并自动渲染为显示就绪的文本。引用地址检索使经文成为库项目，而非粘贴文本。

- **媒体** — 图像和视频：放置在文本后的动态或静态背景，在服务特定时刻播放的剪辑。

许多产品添加更多库类型——公告、礼拜文本、导入的幻灯片集、图片——但歌曲、经文和媒体是常驻三要素。

**2. 服务演示。** 中心工作对象是针对一次日期服务场合的有序提示列表，通过从库中拖拽项目并按照服务顺序排列而组装。术语因产品而异——日程、演示、提示、服务——但结构相同：一个序列。
definition.rules:
### The audience output shows only what is live

The structural guarantee of the Type: nothing from the operator's view — cue lists, searches, previews — leaks to the congregation's screens. Products reinforce this with separate output windows and simplified operator modes that hide editing machinery during the service.

### The cue list is a plan, not a script

The service routinely departs from the plan (an extra song, an unplanned reading). The software therefore treats the cue list as a starting point: on-the-fly retrieval from the library and free navigation within and across items are first-class behaviors, not exceptions.

### Lyric blocks are stepped, not scrolled

A song is displayed block by block under operator control, in step with the singing — the operator, not a timer, advances verse and chorus. (Timed auto-advance exists for announcement loops and pre-service sequences, which are not congregational singing.)

### Scripture is retrieved by reference and rendered automatically

The operator types a reference; the product produces display-ready text from the selected translation. Translation availability and licensing vary by product and plan; some products display two translations side-by-side.

### Projected lyrics carry copyright obligations

Displaying copyrighted songs publicly requires copyright information on screen and usage reporting to licensing bodies. Mature products automate both — copyright data arrives with imported lyrics, and usage is reported automatically. This is a compliance behavior wired into the display loop, not a separate module.

### Content is reused, not discarded

The library accumulates across services and years; a song added once is available forever after. Services are kept and cloned; the weekly rhythm starts from the library and last week's service, not from a blank file.
definition.rules_zh:
### 观众输出仅显示现场内容

该类型的结构性保证：操作员视图中的任何内容——提示列表、搜索、预览——都不会泄露到会众的屏幕。产品通过单独的输出窗口和在礼拜期间隐藏编辑机制的简化操作员模式来强化这一点。

### 提示列表是计划，而非脚本

礼拜通常会偏离计划（额外的歌曲、计划外的诵读）。因此，软件将提示列表视为起点：从库中即时检索和在项目内及项目间自由导航是一级行为，而非例外。

### 歌词块是分步显示，而非滚动

歌曲在操作员控制下逐块显示，与演唱同步——由操作员而非计时器推进诗节和副歌。（计时自动推进用于公告循环和礼拜前序列，这些不是会众歌唱。）

### 经文按参考检索并自动渲染

操作员输入参考；产品根据所选译本生成可供显示的文本。译本可用性和许可因产品和计划而异；有些产品并排显示两种译本。

### 投影歌词带有版权义务

公开展示受版权保护的歌曲需要在屏幕上显示版权信息并向许可机构报告使用情况。成熟产品会自动完成这两项——版权数据随导入的歌词一起到达，使用情况自动报告。这是融入显示循环的合规行为，而非一个独立模块。

### 内容被重用，而非丢弃

库跨礼拜和年份积累；添加一次的歌曲可永久使用。服务被保留和克隆；每周的节奏从库开始

definition.name: Convention / Exhibition Management
definition.overview:
A **Convention / Exhibition Management** application is the show organizer's operating system for producing an exhibition, trade show, or convention. It centers on a structure that generic event software does not have: the exhibition floor, laid out as a plan of individually identified and individually sellable booth or space units, and the exhibitor population whose paid participation fills that floor. Around this core the system sells and assigns space under contract, coordinates exhibitors through a self-service portal, delivers the audience through registration and attendee-facing discovery surfaces, and closes the loop by reporting leads and outcomes back to exhibitors so they rebook for the next edition.

The defining core is therefore:

```text
Show (produced, dated, venue-bound occasion, typically recurring in editions)
└── Exhibitor population (companies and organizations paying to participate)
    └── Exhibition floor as sellable space inventory
        (floor plan decomposed into identified booths/spaces with availability states)
        └── Space allocation binding an exhibitor to specific space
            (application or selection → assignment → contract/payment)
```

Remove the sellable floor and its exhibitor commerce, and what remains is a general event management platform. Remove the exhibitor population, and what remains is a venue booking or diagramming tool. The coupling of show, exhibitors, floor inventory, and space allocation is what makes this a distinct Application Type.

Exhibitions and conventions are treated here as one Type because real products serve both under one roof: the floor-shaped trade show and the session-shaped convention share the same exhibitor commerce spine, and session/program machinery appears as a standard layer when the event format includes an education program.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **会议/展览管理** 应用程序是展览组织者用于制作展览会、交易会或会议的操作系统。它围绕着一个通用事件软件所不具备的结构：展厅平面，被规划为单独标识和可单独销售的展位或空间单元，以及付费参与并填满该平面的参展商群体。围绕这个核心，系统在合同下销售和分配空间，通过自助服务门户协调参展商，通过注册和面向与会者的发现界面吸引观众，并通过向参展商报告潜客和成果来完成闭环，以便他们为下一届重新预订。

因此，其定义性的核心结构是：

```text
展览（被制作的、有日期的、受场地限制的活动，通常以届次形式循环出现）
└── 参展商群体（付费参与的公司和组织）
    └── 作为可销售空间库存的展厅平面
        （平面图分解为已标识且有可用状态的展位/空间）
            └── 将参展商与特定空间绑定的空间分配
                （申请或选择 → 分配 → 合同/支付）
```

移除可销售的展厅平面及其参展商商业活动，剩下的就是一个通用事件管理平台。移除参展商群体，剩下的就是一个场地预订或绘图工具。展览、参展商、平面库存和空间分配的结合，使得这成为一个独特的 **应用程序类型**。

这里的展览会和会议被视为一种类型，因为真实的产品在同一个屋檐下服务于两者：平面布局的交易会和会议议程式的会议共享相同的参展商商业支柱，当活动形式包含教育项目时，会议/议程机制则作为一个标准层出现。
definition.dc: Everything lives inside a **show** — a named, dated, venue-bound occasion. Shows recur, and the recurring edition is an economic fact of the Type: a show's value is its exhibitor base, and the sales cycle for the next edition typically begins before or during the current one. Some products therefore treat the show portfolio — many editions, many shows — as a first-class management layer.
definition.dc_zh: 一切围绕一个**展会**展开——即有名称、日期、场馆的特定活动。展会具有周期性，而其续期版本是该类型的经济基础：展会的价值在于其展商基础，下一届展会的销售周期通常在当前展会期间或之前启动。因此，部分产品会将展会组合——跨越多届、多个展会——视为一等管理层次进行处理。
definition.rules:
- **One space, one exhibitor at a time.** The floor inventory cannot be double-sold: an allocation holds or consumes the space, and the same availability state drives both the organizer's sales console and the public-facing plan. Products add hold and lock mechanics to protect spaces during negotiation and to prevent accidental modification of confirmed layouts.
- **Confirmed space follows recorded commitment.** Assignment and the exhibitor's purchase are connected: applications or selections lead to contracts and payment, and the exhibitor's standing (balance, signed terms) gates what is confirmed and what is merely requested. Exact mechanics vary by product and show policy.
- **The floor plan is audience-scoped.** Different populations see different versions of the same plan: attendees get navigation-oriented maps (exhibitor locations, amenities); exhibitors get detail useful for selecting space (venue entrances, utility locations, columns); contractors get production-ready drawings. Maturity of this separation varies by product; the underlying pattern — one plan, many views — is the structural point.
- **Exhibitor content flows under organizer control.** Exhibitors author their own listings and content, but deadlines, approval, and visibility are organizer-managed: the public directory and floor plan present what the organizer has released.
- **Lead data is generated by exhibitors, governed by the organizer.** Badge scanning happens at the booth, but the data model, consent posture, and export plumbing are provided by the show's system, and lead volume/quality is a headline outcome the organizer reports on.
- **Registration may be native or an integration seam.** The exhibition-specific system can own registration, but in the researched market it equally often integrates a dedicated registration platform; the exhibition machinery does not depend on owning the attendee funnel.
- **The edition is a cycle, not a one-off.** Rebooking, renewal, and retention are structural: sales activity for a future edition can begin on-site during the current one, and exhibitor records persist across editions as the show's core asset.
definition.rules_zh:
- **一个空间，同一时间只能分配给一个参展商。** 展厅库存不能被重复销售：一次分配会占用或消耗该空间，相同的可用状态同时驱动组织者的销售控制台和面向公众的计划。产品会增加预留和锁定机制，以在谈判期间保护空间，并防止对已确认布局的意外修改。
- **确认的空间遵循已记录的承诺。** 分配与参展商的购买行为相关联：申请或选择会导向合同和支付，而参展商的状态（余额、已签署条款）决定了什么是已确认的，什么仅仅是已请求的。具体机制因产品和展览政策而异。
- **平面图是分受众呈现的。** 不同群体看到同一平面图的不同版本：与会者获得以导航为导向的地图（参展商位置、设施）；参展商获得对选择空间有用的信息（场地入口、公共设施位置、柱子）；承包商获得可直接用于施工的图纸。这种区分的成熟度因产品而异；其底层模式——一份平面图，多种视图——是其结构要点。
- **参展商内容的发布受组织者控制。** 参展商自行撰写其列表和内容，但截止日期、审批和可见性由组织者管理：公开目录和展厅平面图展示的是组织者已发布的内容。
- **潜客数据由参展商生成，但由组织者管理。** 徽章扫描发生在展位，但数据模型、同意条款和导出管道由展览系统提供，潜客数量/质量是组织者报告的关键成果。
- **注册可以是原生的，也可以是一个集成点。** 专用于展览的系统可以拥有注册功能，但在所研究的市场中，它同样经常与外部注册系统集成。

definition.name: Event Credential / Badge Management
definition.overview:
An **Event Credential / Badge Management** application designs, produces, personalizes, issues, and maintains the credentials — badges, encoded cards, and digital passes — that identify people at an event and distinguish what they are there as: attendee, staff or crew, speaker, exhibitor, VIP, or press. In many products the credential also carries access meaning, determining which sessions or zones its holder may enter.

The badge is a dual-purpose object: it is the holder's public identity surface (name, organization, role, brand) and the operator's instrument of control (a scannable, revocable, replaceable record of who is present and what they are entitled to). An application of this Type is built around managing that object — not around selling admission, not around capturing registrations, and not around running the event app.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
The event's credential-type program
└── Holder assignment records (person ↔ event ↔ credential type)
    └── Design-to-artifact rendering (template + holder data → badge/pass)
        └── Issuance and replacement operations (pre-print or on-demand)
```

Registration, ticketing, agenda, and engagement systems surround it and feed it; remove the produced credential and its issuance, and what remains is one of those other Types.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**活动凭证/证件管理**应用程序负责设计、制作、个性化、发放和维护用于标识活动参与者的凭证——徽章、编码卡和数字通行证——并区分参与者身份：参会者、工作人员或团队成员、演讲者、参展商、贵宾或媒体。在许多产品中，凭证还承载访问权限含义，决定持有者可进入哪些会议或区域。

徽章是一个双用途物品：它是持有者的公共身份展示面（姓名、组织、角色、品牌），也是运营方的管控工具（可扫描、可撤销、可替换的在场人员及其权限记录）。此类应用程序围绕管理该对象构建——而非围绕销售入场资格、捕捉注册信息或运行活动应用。

定义核心是刻意精简的：

```text
活动的凭证类型体系
└── 持有者分配记录（人员 ↔ 活动 ↔ 凭证类型）
    └── 从设计到实物的呈现（模板 + 持有者数据 → 徽章/通行证）
        └── 发放与更换操作（预印或按需）
```

注册、票务、日程和参与系统围绕其运行并提供数据；若移除生成的凭证及其发放，剩余部分即属于其他类型。
definition.dc:
**1. The credential-type program.** The event defines a set of holder categories. The category is the master switch of the whole system: it determines which design layout is used, which data appears on the credential, which color or medium marks the holder at a glance, and — commonly — what the holder may access. A category set may be as small as a single "attendee" type for a small meeting; it grows into multi-category programs (attendees, speakers, staff, exhibitors, press, VIPs) as events scale. Without categories and their consequences, the software degenerates into label printing.

**2. Holder assignment records.** Each credential is anchored to an identified person bound to the event under one category. Holder records arrive from registration data, imports, or on-site capture (walk-ins), and are maintained over the event's life: edited, moved between categories, voided, replaced. The record — not the piece of paper — is the system of record; the badge is its rendered projection. This is why a badge can be reprinted at any time from current data.

**3. Design-to-artifact rendering.** Per-category design templates merge holder data into the produced artifact: a physical badge (sheet-printed or on-demand thermal/plastic), an encoded credential (QR/barcode, RFID-class media), or a digital pass in an app or wallet. Preview before production is standard because the badge is a brand surface as much as an operational one. One and the same holder data commonly renders into adjacent artifacts too — participant lists, place or escort cards — which is why design and data are kept separate.

**4. Issuance and replacement operations.** Production and handover are managed, stateful operations: badges are either produced in batches before the event or printed on demand at the moment of check-in; either way, the system tracks that a person was issued a credential, and it reissues when credentials are lost, damaged, or issued with stale information. Reprint-at-the-desk for lost badges is a routine, designed-for operation across the sampled products, from academic tools to enterprise platforms.
definition.dc_zh:
**1. 凭证类型程序。** 活动定义一组持有者类别。类别是整个系统的主开关：它决定使用哪种设计布局、凭证上显示哪些数据、哪种颜色或介质让持有者一目了然，以及——通常——持有者可以访问什么。类别集可以小到一个小会议的单一“与会者”类型；随着活动规模扩大，它发展为多类别程序（与会者、演讲者、工作人员、参展商、媒体、贵宾）。没有类别及其后果，软件退化为标签打印。

**2. 持有者分配记录。** 每个凭证都锚定到一个在活动下绑定到一个类别的已识别人员。持有者记录来自注册数据、导入或现场捕获（临时入场），并在活动生命周期内维护：编辑、在类别之间移动、作废、替换。记录——而不是那张纸——是记录系统；徽章是其渲染投影。这就是为什么徽章可以随时从当前数据重新打印。

**3. 设计到产物的渲染。** 每个类别的设计模板将持有者数据合并到生成的产物中：物理徽章（ sheet-printed 或按需热敏/塑料）、编码凭证（QR/条码、RFID类介质）或应用或钱包中的数字通行证。生产前预览是标准做法，因为徽章是b
definition.rules:
- **The category drives everything.** Change a holder's category and the design, the printed data, and (where present) the access entitlements all follow. Nothing about the badge is edited freehand on the artifact itself; all changes happen on the record.
- **The record, not the paper, is the truth.** Badges are re-renderable at any time from current data; a reprint is a rendering operation, not a correction. On-demand printing exists precisely to keep the artifact synchronized with late edits.
- **Issuance is a state change, and it is logged.** Recording arrival is an attributed, dated action, and the desk's ability to perform it is a governed permission — one researched product explicitly recommends a separate system account per desk so actions can be attributed afterward.
- **Fee status gates the express path.** Commonly, arrival processing interacts with payment state: some products disable express check-in until fees are settled and force an explicit confirmation, while others capture payment at the desk. Unpaid and walk-in cases are deliberately routed to special handling instead of succeeding silently.
- **Desk roles are deliberately limited.** Where role models are documented, issuance staff can search, check in, and print, but cannot see fee details, take payments, alter registrations, or undo cancellations — those belong to administrator roles.
- **Access enforcement is scale-dependent.** Session/zone admit-deny machinery appears where events are large or security-conscious; its absence does not disqualify a product from the Type, and its presence does not change the defining core.
- **The door must keep working.** Check-in and badging are treated as availability-critical surfaces; several products document continued operation through connectivity loss.
- **Data flows back out.** Check-in and attendance data is kept as the event's attendance record and pushed to CRM/marketing systems, closing the loop that started at registration.
definition.rules_zh:
- **类别驱动一切。** 更改持有者类别后，设计、打印数据以及（若存在）访问权限全部随之改变。徽章实物本身没有任何自由编辑；所有更改都发生在记录上。
- **记录而非纸张才是真相。** 徽章可随时根据当前数据重新呈现；重新打印是呈现操作，而非更正。按需打印正是为保持实物与后期编辑同步而存在。
- **发放是状态变更，并会记录在案。** 记录到达是带归属、带日期的操作，柜台执行此操作的能力是受控权限——某款调研产品明确建议为每个柜台设置独立系统账户，以便后续操作可追溯。
- **费用状态是快速通道的门控。** 通常，到达处理与支付状态交互：某些产品在费用结清前禁用快速签到并要求明确确认，另一些则在柜台捕获支付。未支付和临时参与者刻意进入特殊处理，而非静默通过。
- **柜台角色刻意受限。** 在有角色模型文档的产品中，发放人员可搜索、签到和打印，但无法查看费用详情、收取支付、修改注册或撤销取消——这些属于管理员角色。
- **访问执行取决于规模。** 会议/区域准入机制出现在大型或安全敏感活动中；其缺失并不妨碍产品属于此类型，其存在也不改变定义核心。
- **门口必须持续运作。** 签到和发证被视为可用性关键界面；多款产品文档记录了在连接中断时继续运营。

definition.name: Event Mobile App
definition.overview:
An **Event Mobile App** is an application that an event's organizer publishes for that event, and that the event's attendees use on their personal mobile devices as their pocket companion to the event — before, during, and after it. The organizer fills the app with the event's program, people, places, and announcements; attendees open it to find what is on and where, plan their own schedule, stay informed of changes, and participate through networking and engagement features.

The defining core is small:

```text
Event-bound app container
└── Organizer-authored event content
    └── Attendee companion use across the event cycle
```

Everything else the market associates with the category — personal agendas, attendee networking, live polls and Q&A, gamification, interactive maps, sponsor promotion, analytics, digital badges, session streams — is standard or optional capability layered on that spine, not what makes the product an event app. A bare app with the event's schedule, maps, and info pages, updated by the organizer and carried by attendees, is fully in-type; a full networking and engagement suite simply extends it.

The smartphone is the Type's characteristic surface — the category exists because attendees carry a personal, installable, always-with-them device — and most products also ship a web version of the same app from the same content. When the center of gravity moves to the organizer's side (registration, ticketing, check-in operations, program building), the product becomes one of the neighboring event Types instead; the event app is the attendee-facing published surface those Types feed.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**活动移动应用**是由活动组织者为该活动发布，并由活动参与者在其个人移动设备上使用的应用程序，作为他们在活动前、活动中和活动后的贴身伴侣。组织者将活动的议程、人物、地点和公告填充到应用中；参与者打开它来查看活动内容和地点、规划自己的日程、及时了解变更，并通过社交和参与功能进行互动。

其定义的核心是简洁的：

```text
事件绑定应用容器
└── 组织者编写的活动内容
    └── 参与者在整个活动周期内的伴侣式使用
```

市场上与该类别相关的所有其他功能——个人议程、参与者社交、实时投票和问答、游戏化、交互式地图、赞助商推广、分析、数字徽章、环节直播——都是在此主干之上添加的标准或可选能力，并非使产品成为活动应用的核心要素。一个仅包含活动日程、地图和信息页面，由组织者更新、参与者随身携带的简单应用，完全符合该类型定义；而一套完整的社交和互动套件只是对其的扩展。

智能手机是该类型的特征平台——该类别的存在是因为参与者携带一个个人的、可安装的、始终随身的设备——并且大多数产品也会从相同内容中发布同一应用的网络版本。当重心转移到组织者一侧（注册、票务、签到操作、议程构建）时，该产品就转变为相邻的活动类型之一；活动应用则是那些类型所供给的、面向参与者的已发布界面。
definition.dc:
```text
Event-bound app container
   (an application instance published for one event,
    or an organizer-defined set of events)
   ↓ filled with
Organizer-authored event content
   (program · people · places · information · announcements)
   ↓ used by
The attendee's companion session
   (personal, mobile, spanning before → during → after the event)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as an event app:

- **Event-bound container.** The app exists for a specific event occasion — or, in container-app variants, for an organizer's defined set of events — and everything inside is scoped to that occasion. The organizer creates, configures, and publishes the app instance per event. Without the event binding, the product is a generic app builder or a generic community app.
- **Organizer-authored content.** The organizer composes what the app presents: the program (sessions, agenda), the people (speakers, attendees, exhibitors and sponsors), the places (venue and campus maps, room locations), the information (logistics, FAQs, handbooks), and the running announcements. Attendees consume this published content and act on it — they bookmark, message, and respond — but they do not author the app's structure. Without organizer authorship, the product is a social or content application.
- **Attendee companion use.** The primary user is the event's attendee, on their own mobile device, for whom the app is the pocket companion to one event: what is on now and next, where to go, what changed, whom to meet. Without the attendee as the primary user, the product is organizer-side event management software; without the app container, it is an event website.
definition.dc_zh:
活动绑定的应用容器
   （为一个特定活动发布，或由组织者定义的一组活动，
    所构成的应用实例）
   ↓ 内容填充为
活动组织者编写的内容
   （日程 · 人员 · 场地 · 资讯 · 动态公告）
   ↓ 由以下对象使用
参会者的伴生应用会话
   （个性化的、移动端的、贯穿活动前→中→后的使用过程）

三个核心属性。若移除其中任意一项，该产品将无法被识别为活动应用：

- **活动绑定容器。** 该应用为特定活动场合而存在——或在容器化应用变体中，为组织者定义的一组活动而存在——其内部的一切都服务于该场合。组织者为每个活动创建、配置并发布应用实例。若没有这种活动绑定，该产品就是一个通用应用构建器或通用社区应用。
- **组织者编写内容。** 应用呈现的内容由组织者编排：日程（会议、议程）、人员（演讲者、参会者、展商与赞助商）、场地（场馆与校园地图、房间位置）、资讯（后勤、常见问题、手册）以及实时动态公告。参会者消费这些已发布的内容并据此行动——他们收藏、发消息、参与回应——但他们并不负责构建应用本身的结构。若没有组织者的编写主导权，该产品就是一个社交或内容类应用。
- **参会者伴生使用。** 主要用户是活动参会者，他们在活动前后及期间使用该应用来完成信息获取、互动交流、日程管理等一系列随身事务。
definition.rules:
- **The organizer owns the content; attendees personalize it.** Attendees choose sessions, message people, and respond — they never reshape the program or the app's structure. The personal agenda is always a derived view of the published program.
- **One edit, every surface.** The app, its web version, and commonly companion displays draw from the same content the organizer maintains; a correction propagates everywhere rather than forking. Push notifications exist precisely because some changes must reach attendees actively, not passively.
- **The app is published per event and has a managed lifecycle.** It goes live while being built, runs through the event, and remains accessible afterwards under rules the product and organizer define — archive, sunset, or continuation as a year-round space.
- **Access is a configured policy, not a constant.** The same Type spans open no-login guides and strictly gated apps; where attendees sign in, they commonly authenticate against the event's registration records, and profile visibility is an organizer-controlled privacy surface.
- **The app consumes identity; it does not create it.** Attendee records, tickets, and check-in entitlements originate in the registration and badge side of the event stack; the app renders and uses them (QR codes, check-in codes, digital badges) rather than owning the intake.
- **Engagement flows back to the organizer.** Adoption, session interest, messages, and sponsor interactions are recorded and reported — the app is also a measurement instrument for the event team and its sponsors.
- **Personal data is handled under event privacy rules.** Mature products carry privacy-policy display, consent, and data-deletion machinery for attendee data, consistent with the event's obligations.
definition.rules_zh:
- **组织者拥有内容；参与者对其进行个性化。** 参与者选择环节、给人们发信息并回应——他们永远不会重塑议程或应用的结构。个人议程始终是已发布议程的一个衍生视图。
- **一次编辑，所有界面更新。** 应用、其网络版本以及通常的配套显示设备，都使用组织者维护的同一内容；更正会传播到各处，而不是产生分歧。推送通知的存在正是为了主动地而非被动地让某些变更触达参与者。
- **应用按活动发布，并拥有受管理的生命周期。** 它在构建过程中上线，在活动期间运行，并在活动后根据产品和组织者定义的规则保持可访问——归档、下线或延续为全年空间。
- **访问权限是配置的策略，而非固定值。** 同一类型涵盖无需登录的开放指南和严格管控的应用；在参与者需要登录的地方，他们通常针对活动的注册记录进行身份验证，并且个人资料可见性是由组织者控制的隐私界面。
- **应用消费身份；它并不创建身份。** 参与者记录、门票和签到权限源自活动堆栈的注册和徽章部分；应用呈现和使用它们（二维码、签到码、数字徽章），而非拥有信息输入环节。
- **互动数据反馈回组织者。** 采纳度、环节兴趣、消息和赞助商互动都会被记录和报告——应用也是活动团队及其赞助商的测量工具。
- **个人数据根据活动隐私规则处理。** 成熟的产品具备隐私政策展示、同意和数据删除机制来处理参与者数据，与活动的义务保持一致。

definition.name: Zoo / Aquarium Visitor Operations
definition.name_zh: 动物园/水族馆游客运营
definition.overview:
Zoo and aquarium visitor operations software is the operator-side system of record for a zoological institution's visitor business: it sells and validates admission, runs the membership economy that most zoos and aquariums depend on for repeat revenue, books education programs and group visits, sells capacity-managed animal encounters and tours, records food and retail spending inside the institution, and turns all of it into attendance, revenue, and visitor data the institution manages from.

Its defining core is the admission business: operator-defined admission products, multi-channel sale, recorded transactions that issue entitlements, validation at entry, and on-site spending. This is the same core that attraction management systems serve across all visitor attractions; what this page documents is how that core is shaped, emphasized, and operated in the zoo and aquarium segment — a membership-centric revenue model, education and group sales as a major operational surface, animal encounters sold as session products, and, for most institutions, a nonprofit posture with donations and supporter relationships.

The boundary is equally clear, and the market states it explicitly: this is not the software that manages the animals. Animal records, husbandry, enrichment, and water quality live in collection-management systems — a separate domain that visitor-operations products do not contain. One vendor of zoo visitor software states it verbatim: it is "not a platform for managing zoo animal records."
definition.overview_zh:
动物园和水族馆访客运营软件是这类机构访客业务的运营方记录系统：它销售并验证入场，运营大多数动物园和水族馆赖以生存的重复收入来源的会员经济，预订教育项目和团体参观，销售容量管理的动物互动体验和导览，记录机构内部的食品和零售消费，并将所有这些转化为机构赖以管理的出勤、收入和访客数据。

其定义核心是入场业务：运营方定义的入场产品、多渠道销售、发行权益的已记录交易、入口验证以及现场消费。这正是景点管理系统在所有访客景点中服务的相同核心；本页面文档记录的内容是该核心在动物园和水族馆细分领域中如何被塑造、强调和运营——一个以会员为中心的收入模型、教育和团体销售作为主要运营层面、动物互动作为会话产品销售，以及对大多数机构而言，具有捐赠和支持者关系的非营利姿态。

边界同样明确，并且市场已明确声明：这不是管理动物的软件。动物记录、饲养管理、丰容和水质数据属于收藏管理系统——这是一个独立的领域，访客运营产品不包含其中。一家动物园访客软件供应商明确表示：它“不是一个管理动物园动物记录的平台”。
definition.dc:
```text
Admission product (day ticket / membership / group ticket)
  → sold through a channel (gate POS, online, kiosk, call center, reseller)
    → recorded transaction issues entitlements
      → validated at entry (scan of ticket, QR, or membership credential)
        → the attendance record
+ on-site spending (food, retail, extras) recorded against the same operation
```

Four properties hold this together:

- **Admission products defined by the institution.** The zoo decides what admission means: a dated or open-dated day ticket, an annual membership, a group ticket, a bundled package. Without operator-defined admission products there is no visitor business to run.
- **Sale produces recorded transactions and entitlements.** Every channel — gate, online, kiosk, phone, reseller — lands in the same transaction record and issues redeemable entitlements.
- **Validation at entry produces attendance.** The scan (barcode, QR code, wristband, membership card) is both the guest's gate and the institution's attendance count.
- **On-site spending recorded against the same operation.** Food, retail, and extras flow into the same reporting spine, so the institution sees attendance and per-visitor spending together.

The core is not animal-shaped. Nothing in it references exhibits, enclosures, or species — which is why the same structure serves museums, theme parks, and water parks. The animals are the draw; admission is the transaction.
definition.dc_zh:
门票产品（日票/会员/团体票）
  → 通过渠道（闸机POS、线上、自助机、呼叫中心、分销商）销售
    → 记录交易并产生权益凭证
      → 在入口核验（扫描门票、二维码或会员凭证）
        → 生成客流记录
+ 现场消费（餐饮、零售、附加服务）记录在同一个运营体系中

四个核心属性维系此结构：
- **由运营机构定义的门票产品**。动物园决定门票的含义：日期票或开放式日票、年卡会员、团体票、套餐包。没有运营方定义的门票产品，游客业务便无从谈起。
- **销售产生交易记录与权益凭证**。所有渠道——闸机、线上、自助机、电话、分销商——均归入同一交易记录，并生成可兑换的权益凭证。
- **入口核验生成客流数据**。扫码（条码、二维码、手环、会员卡）既是游客的通行凭证，也是机构的客流计数依据。
- **现场消费记录于同一运营体系**。餐饮、零售和附加服务均汇入同一报表体系，使机构能同时查看客流与人均消费。

核心逻辑与动物形态无关。其定义不涉及展品、围栏或物种——因此同一架构亦可服务于博物馆、主题公园与水上乐园。
definition.rules:
- **Entitlement validity governs everything downstream.** A ticket, membership, or session works only where and while its entitlement says it does. Every control point checks the same entitlement state.
- **A membership is an annual entitlement with recognition, not just a product.** It admits the member (often with named-adult rules and photo checks), carries benefits (parking, discounts, event access), and typically excludes separately ticketed events and some school-group periods — exclusions institutions publish in their own membership terms.
- **Reciprocal admission is an external network.** A member's free or discounted admission at other zoos and aquariums is governed by an inter-institution reciprocity list, not by this system alone; the system's role is recognizing the visiting member and applying the agreed benefit.
- **Capacity is shared and actively managed.** Timed-entry slots, encounter sessions, and member reservations draw on the same capacity pools; peak-day capacity is a configuration surface, not an afterthought.
- **Group bookings carry balances and headcounts.** A school group's reservation can be confirmed with a deposit, adjusted for headcount on the day, and settled for the balance — the group ticket is one entitlement covering many people.
- **Encounters are entitlements too.** A session booking is validated like admission; over-booking is prevented by the same capacity machinery.
- **Donations attach to transactions in the nonprofit posture.** The ask happens at checkout and other touchpoints; the donation lands in the same record spine as the sale.
- **Money is recorded per revenue center.** Admission, membership, education, food, retail, and extras each land in their own reporting line.
- **Animal records live elsewhere.** Visitor operations holds no animal data; the institution's collection-management system is a separate system of record. Where the two worlds meet at all, it is through public-facing content (exhibit information in apps), not through shared operational records.
definition.rules_zh:
- **权益有效性决定后续一切。** 票据、会员资格或会话仅在其权益声明的地点和时间有效。每个控制点都检查相同的权益状态。
- **会员资格是一种带有识别功能的年度权益，而不仅仅是一个产品。** 它允许会员入场（通常有实名成人规则和照片检查），携带权益（停车、折扣、活动参与权），并且通常排除单独售票的活动和一些学校团体时段——这些排除条款由机构在其会员条款中公布。
- **互认入场是一个外部网络。** 会员在其他动物园和水族馆的免费或优惠入场由机构间互认名单管理，而非仅由本系统管理；系统的角色是识别来访会员并应用约定的权益。
- **容量是共享并主动管理的。** 定时入场时段、互动体验会话和会员预订使用相同的容量池；高峰日容量是一个配置层面，而非事后考虑。
- **团体预订包含余额和人数。** 学校团体的预订可以用押金确认，在当日调整人数，并结算尾款——团体票据是一个涵盖多人的权益。
- **互动体验也是权益。** 会话预订像入场一样被验证；超额预订通过相同的容量机制防止。
- **在非营利姿态下，捐赠附加于交易。** 请求发生在结账和其他接触点；捐赠落入与销售相同的记录主干。
- **资金按收入中心记录。** 入场、会员、教育、食品、零售和附加项各自计入其自己的报告行。
- **动物记录存在于其他地方。** 访客运营
